items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以爱丁堡皇家植物园一棵百年萨巴尔棕榈的倒下为叙事起点，由歌手兼词曲作者卡琳·波尔沃特与声音设计师皮帕·墨菲共同创作，并融入舞台演出与书籍。作品以人声、钢琴和克制的环境音效展开，旋律带有苏格兰风笛般的缓慢哀感，重复的歌词与音乐片段形成记忆锚点。编曲虽简朴，却在亲密感与历史、自然的宏大主题之间取得平衡。结尾揭示树的真实身份及其新生植株，为专辑增添关于时间、延续与希望的转折。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼音乐档案学者Dominique Cravic与Robert Crumb共同发起的Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，是其第五张作品。整张唱片由27首短曲组成，乐器阵容极为庞杂，从手风琴、萨克斯、班卓琴、尤克里里到Theremin音乐锯甚至风笛哨管均被纳入，试图复原早期78转唱片时代的声响质感。Cravic以近似法国老式香颂的方式演绎，配以手风琴主导的伴奏，整体呈现出复古拼贴的气质。曲目来源跨越百年，从1925年的《Ukulele Lady》到向法国抵抗运动偶像Juliette Gréco致敬的同名曲，再到对《Smoke Gets in Your Eyes》《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典的重构，乐评将其比作Dan Hicks式的不可归类之作。乐手大多年过七旬，但展现出高度投入与对旧时音乐风格的严谨研究态度。

items._cn_summary: Brama的专辑《La Raive》以"迷幻力量三人组"自居，融合快节奏器乐迷幻段落与传统欧洲手摇风琴。第二轨《Belou de Jorn》末段是全专最值得玩味的时刻：四分钟的器乐密集推进后，鼓组与各声部逐渐剥离消散，最终只剩一把手摇风琴的孤独和弦浮现，这一反差处理构成专辑的核心戏剧张力。整体策略是在高速迷 psychedelic 框架中植入传统欧洲民间乐器，与现代摇滚编制形成对话。Airfono属于欧洲独立小厂牌，发行定位偏地下。专辑在传统乐器与迷幻摇滚的跨界处理上有一定想法，但对用户偏好的实验前卫、爵士即兴或电子深领域而言，仍停留在较为常规的融合层面，深度实验性有限。

Listen to Harris' 21-minute piece for Constellation below. Kranky will release Music For... The post Liz Harris Plots New Release of Soundtrack Work appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Liz Harris（艺名Grouper）通过长期合作的独立厂牌Kranky发行最新配乐合辑，收录两首长篇作品，分别是为2023年纪录片《We Exhale》和2024年影像作品《Constellation》创作。前者探讨人类对罗讷河数世纪的拦截与污染，后者由Makino导演通过既存影像与记忆碎片的重新编排探讨意义的生成过程。Harris以声音与影像的深度互动著称，她的配乐并非简单的背景衬托，而是与画面形成同等重量的对位关系。作为小厂牌发行的声音艺术向长篇配乐，作品延续了她标志性的氛围与即兴结合路线，面向实验音乐与影像艺术爱好者。原文为新闻发布性质，缺乏具体的声音分析与评论深度。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — The debut album of the progressive rock supergroup consisting of Keith Emerson of THE NICE, Greg Lake of KING CRIMSON and Carl Palmer of ATOMIC ROOSTER. A bold statement of what was to come, with the band incorporating their classical and jazz background to their rock music.The album is a mix of original songs (Take a pebble, The three fates, Tank & Lucky man) and rock arrangements of classical music (The barbarian & Knife-edge.) Keith Emerson is the key figure of the album of course, with his bombastic playing. Carl Palmer is a really hard hitter and delivers a great drum solo as well on the track "Tank". Lake's voice is heart-warming as always, but the man can deliver some amazing bass lines as well. The album is characterized by top flight musicianship, but unfortunately not top flight songwriting, at least at some parts of it. Despite that, it is a strong album, and any album with "Take a pebble" on, is worth owning.
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / classical rock
items._cn_summary: 这是前卫摇滚超级组合的首张专辑，三位成员分别来自不同名噪一时的英国摇滚乐队，将各自的古典与爵士背景融入摇滚框架。专辑由原创作品与古典改编并置：原创部分以温暖的人声、贝斯线条和钢琴炫技为骨架，改编部分则将穆索尔斯基、扬纳切克等古典作曲家的作品以摇滚编制重新诠释。鼓手卡尔·帕尔默在《Tank》中贡献了一段硬朗的鼓独奏，键盘手基思·爱默生的演奏风格占据主导，编曲铺排宏大，乐手演奏水准精湛。然而评论指出，专辑在作曲层面存在短板，部分段落未能达到演奏所展现的高度。整体而言，这是一张以器乐技术和古典跨界为核心、奠定乐队后续方向的作品。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — From the title which translates loosely to "loose woman" to the cover of a quasi-mythical physically well appointed female to the generally erotic lyrical themes of the trad and original numbers presented here, TARUJEN SAARI's second album is probably the merriest of their discography. The ensemble continues to present renditions of well known songs from the British Isles as well as their homeland, and once again in each case they offer a novel interpretation.Closest comparisons would be with the more politically serious MABSANT from Wales and GALAHAD from Germany, with the usual British Isles (including JETHRO TULL at their folkiest) and Breton (BERNARD BENOIT) suspects of course, and, in one track ("Lampolan Vintilla"), the as yet unformed SANGRE DE MUERDAGO. "Y� viel� on" has a go at the very first track on the very first CLANNAD album in a manner which, superior or not, fits better on this album than on that Donegal group's debut. It's a good deal more rocking with menacing fiddles. The last 2 songs respectively revisit "Tam Lin" (best known as a FAIRPORT song) and "The Twelve Witches" (STEELEYE SPAN) and to me are unrecognizable from the versions I know, with only the first somewhat signaled by its many verses. It's much more mysterious with whistles and whispered lyrics for the first part but, without following along the Finnish lyrics, I find it stays on past closing time, while I have no issues with "Twelve Witches" at all, a typically dire lyric made joyous, even in Finnish!For the rest, it's all at least good, with the best being "Hepsankaika" which introduces our character "type", the saucy fiddle-heavy "Neidon Kielto", the cello infused and at least R rated "Minulta Saisit", and the seize the day whistled exuberance of "Lampolan Vintill�".Our protagonist can succeed in seducing even the most hardened of us from track one, and isn't that her goal? She does get a lot of help from a band that is a lot more disciplined than she.

items._cn_summary: 这是芬兰乐队TARUJEN SAARI的第二张专辑，以轻松欢快的方式演绎英伦三岛与芬兰本土的传统民谣。乐队对经典曲目如《Tam Lin》和《The Twelve Witches》进行了全新的诠释，前者以口哨与低语营造神秘氛围，后者将原本严肃的歌词转化为欢乐的芬兰语版本。编曲中突出小提琴、口哨和大提琴等器乐元素，部分曲目带有较强的摇滚感与不协和的小提琴线条。评论提及与威尔士乐队MABSANT和德国GALAHAD的风格接近，歌词主题围绕一个虚构的女性形象展开，兼具传统民谣基底与个性化的改编视角。专辑整体保持民俗根脉，但通过器乐编配和语言转换提供了不同于原曲的聆听体验。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — And the creators of and tour guides to alternate worldscapes press on! Amazing! 1. "Guardstones" (6:40) a rambling piece that sounds more like a soundtrack piece for a documentary on Amazonian rainforests. Nice bass and drum interplay from Corey Wallace and Pat Garvey in the fourth minute. (8.75/10)2. "Space Platform" (5:57) a song that seems to have a built in reset button as it cycles around several times from spacey keyboard rhythm tracks into full-speed free-wheelin' off-road mountain biking craziness over and over again, not just once or twice but five times! Each time as the high-speed craziness melts into spacey observation mode I find myself thinking, "well, that was fun; too bad it's over" but then it returns, wave after wave. Awesome (if a bit familiar surf for the Ozrics). (9/10)3. "Harmonic Mind" (9:12) a song that actually sounds like something from THE PSYCHEDELIC ENSEMBLE: "The Golden King" from 2013's The Tale of the Golden Kings! I know this has to be purely a coincidence but the similarities are multiple and unmistakable. A little heavier with Ed's use of PETE TOWNSEND-like guitar power chords and, later, SynthAxe-like Industrial guitar sounds (think 1980s Allan Holdworth and Three of a Perfect Pair-era Robert Fripp). Eventually the guitar and keyboard work kind of trims and smooths but Pat and Corey are still flying at top speed as if they're in a real hurry to get somewhere--which makes it a challenge for the rest of the band to A) keep up and B) find inspiration. I mean, Silas continues to inject fun and interesting space-jungle sounds and riffs but Ed seems to be struggling with his guitar synthesizer, trying to find creative things to add to the mix. Interesting! (17.6667/20)4. "Malachite" (7:52) a song that seems to have trouble finding an identity. There are good intentions from Pat and Corey, but they're not finding the kind of support that one would hope for: it's as if the two front men are having trouble connecting or finding inspiration from the lines and melodies coming from the rhythm corps. Weird! There are so many instances that remind me of other artist's songs and sounds but there is just this wall preventing anything from congealing! Ed's injection of sitar and Silas' old-school TD synth sound don't work either--but Corey and Pat still seem to be having a great time; it's just too bad that all four couldn't find a connection. Still, I really enjoy just listening to Pat Garvey's enthusiastic and sublime drum play on this one. (13.125/15)5. "Tillamook" (9:11) great long interdimensional atmospheric opening (the drums and bass line don't kick in until the second half of the fourth minute!) then it's scenic highway driving, as usual, as Pat's drums and Corey's bass drive Ed to great guitar heights--but only for an abreviated time as Ed generously gives way to Silas's creative soundmaking, taking us into the forests of the Pacific Northwest and the highways that service them. A pause around 7:30 turns into another rhythm-less underwater keyboard excursion to which Ed adds some tempered and Paul Speer-like guitar riffs. Excellent song! One could not ask for more or better from Ed and the Ozrics! (18.875/20) 6. "Sumipad" (4:54) this one sounds a little traveled: as if I'm hearing a new, updated version of something they've done before (and done well, I might add). The problem is: for any Ozrics lover this is not/never a bad thing: it's great music and a great alternate reality that the band ushers us into. Such a delight! It's so hard for me to imagine someone--anyone--not loving this music! (9.333/10) Total Time 43:46Though it is always a joy to discover/uncover new Ozrics music, there is just enough of a disconnect between the rhythm section and the lead duo on this album to prevent total and satisfactory immersion within the "alternate worlds" that Ed and his crew offer us.A-/4.5 stars; a wonderful exposure to the delightful sonic worlds of Ed Wynne and his Ozric Tentacles though not quite as fully-fleshed out as one might hope. Still, "Tillamook" and "Sumipad" are not to be missed: two additions to the long list of Ozrics' "classics."
items._cn_summary: Ozric Tentacles 的《Harmonic Mind》延续了乐队标志性的太空迷幻摇滚路线，将环境氛围段落与高能量的器乐即兴交替铺陈。专辑中贝斯与鼓的互动构成核心驱动力，键盘与吉他合成器在其上构建层层纹理。吉他手尝试了多种音色，包括西塔琴与八十年代工业感合成器音色，试图在熟悉配方中注入新意，但部分曲目被乐评指出难以凝聚整体认同感，乐队成员之间存在灵感错位。制作中穿插了自然纪录片式的氛围段落，呼应丛林与太平洋西北森林的意象，体现了乐队在场景化器乐探索上的持续尝试。

items.body: Review by Rysiek P. — The following statement might be a bit of an exaggeration, but if one were to single out the most important Argentine - or even, I would venture to say, South American - symphonic rock band, that band would, in my opinion, be Nexus. The roots of this Argentine quintet go back to the 1970s, when a group of students from the capital, Buenos Aires, became fascinated by symphonic rock - a passion that soon led to the band's formation. However, the dream of releasing a full-length album was not realized until the late 1990s, when the group brought out its debut record, *Detr�s del Umbral*, in 1999. Their early releases are characterized by an impressive, monumental sound rich in superb keyboard parts. Powerful, expressive female vocals infuse the music with emotional depth, preventing the sense of "technical excess" or "overloading" that can sometimes plague bands relying heavily on synthesizer and organ elements in their arrangements. Their most obvious influences include the work of ELP (Hammond organ playing), Genesis's middle period (rich, symphonic sound), and Marillion (synthesizer passages). The undisputed turning point in their career was the 2001 album *Metanoia* - in my view, still one of the finest symphonic rock albums ever recorded by a South American band. Its sound is remarkably impressive, driven by rich, monumental keyboard arrangements. The album features outstanding symphonic rock compositions that captivate the listener with numerous stirring mood shifts and magnificent keyboard and guitar solos. The powerful Spanish-language vocals harmonize perfectly with the diverse atmospheres presented throughout the record. *Metanoia* embodies all the elements that make symphonic rock such a compelling genre! Among their later works, the 2011 album *La Divina Comedia*, the following year's *Aire*, and the 2023 release *Insania* all deserve attention and belong in every symphonic rock fan's collection. It is also worth checking out the recently released (2023) live album *Nexus en Concierto / Homenaje a CRUCIS* to see for yourself that the Argentinians are a great live act as well. But let's return to the main reason for this article: the latest album, *1042*, which was officially released on October 2nd of this year. Its release marks the band's 50th anniversary (their first concert took place on July 10, 1976) and features a guest appearance by Gustavo Montesano - bassist and vocalist for the group Crucis. Once again, Nexus takes the listener on a journey of over forty minutes into a realm of extraordinary sounds. Rest assured - after all, this is their tenth full-length album. Be prepared, however, to hear - right from the opening track - fundamental differences between symphonic rock in the European-American sense (which radiates a barrage of endless synthesizers and organs, often accompanied by frenetic, majestic guitar solos) and the symphonic rock of South American bands, which is bombastic yet strangely "soft" and melodic. The track "El Visitante," while serving as an instrumental intro, is also a magnificent example of this specific musical approach. It sounds powerful and assertive, yet simultaneously very melodic - almost "song-like" - with the swaying phrases of slightly subdued synthesizers. South American bands also approach the role of vocals in their music somewhat differently. This is immediately evident in the second track of the new album: "Desiertos" (Deserts) is both a magnificent composition with a perfectly chosen key and one of the release's two standout tracks. The song unfolds at a leisurely pace, and an intriguing music video - available on various platforms - illustrates its lyrical themes. This ballad-like delicacy is further enhanced by the narrative vocal style of Roxy Truccolo, a band member since 2017 (when she contributed to the album *En El Comienzo Del Topos Uranos*). Her vocals were already a superb "bonus" on the band's previous album (*Insania*), but here she sounds magnificent; she adds an element of Gothic mystery to her naturally calm timbre while steering clear of quasi-operatic tones. It is also worth noting that Roxy handles all the bass lines. The track "Sin Saber Del Sol" begins in a somewhat similar fashion. Once again, Roxy's vocals, combined with synthesizers, infuse the track - which is undeniably keyboard-driven - with an atmosphere of tranquility and a certain epic quality. Yet, this is not a composition that flaunts its synthesizer or organ sounds; rather, these elements are seamlessly woven into the musical fabric. They do not demand special attention or compel the listener to hunt for hidden sonic layers; instead, they contribute on equal footing with the vocals and rhythm section to create a composition that feels simultaneously symphonic and non-symphonic. The situation is entirely different with the track "El Otro Lado." Here, synthesizer sounds with a hard-rock edge captivate the listener through their sheer power and staccato chords. It is in this track that the "South American" sound comes closest to the "European" style, with its robust, slightly hard-rock-influenced foundation. In my opinion, the second track that makes the greatest impression on the listener is the composition "Una Ley." It is an epic piece, characterized by sweeping phrasing and melodic flourishes. It features a long instrumental introduction and piano accompaniment, against which every sung verse feels like a deeply sorrowful confession. Six minutes that reach into the deepest recesses of the musical soul. Six minutes of a truly epic musical journey in the finest symphonic style. The final track - "Periplo Del Ego" - showcases the band's improvisational prowess. Naturally, this display unfolds against a backdrop of flawless musical backing. There are Emerson-esque keyboards, powerful drum hits, and a structure entirely driven by the instruments. It is nearly twelve minutes of sheer mastery, allowing each musician to showcase their skills in a way that creates a multidimensional composition - a brilliant example of modern symphonic rock. On the version of the album I own, the band serves up "Teaser Album 1042 - Bonus Track" right at the end - a preview of the record's musical content that had previously appeared here and there as promotional material. It's the album in a nutshell: three minutes containing a bit of everything. Just a nice little extra for the fans. In summary? The album *1042* restores faith in symphonic rock while reminding us that, alongside the familiar varieties, there exists another - the South American kind. It is distinctive, unlike the versions we usually encounter: mellow, song-oriented, lyrical, and epic. A great deal is happening - or is about to happen - in the world of symphonic rock this year. We have already seen a release from The Neal Morse Band, with new albums from The Flower Kings and Neal Morse & The Resonance arriving shortly. The latest offerings from Khatsaturjan and The Samurai of Prog have also shone brightly on the musical horizon. We have only just listened to the new double album from Andy Tillison's The Tangent. It will be difficult to pick a single "best" album this year. That is why I increasingly feel the need to create two separate lists: one for "progressive" albums and another for "unconventional crossover" releases - a move I feel somewhat compelled to make as a "musical Darwinist." This time, it simply won't all fit into one category... (sic!). Published also at MLWZ.pl
items._cn_summary: Nexus 是一支来自阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯克的交响前卫摇滚乐队，其根源可追溯至1976年，以丰富的键盘编排和女性主唱的情感表达为核心特色。乐队早期作品深受ELP（哈蒙德风琴）、Genesis中期和Marillion影响，2001年的《Metanoia》被认为是南美最出色的交响摇滚专辑之一，键盘编排庞大宏伟，西班牙语人声与多样氛围完美契合。2026年发行的第十张录音室专辑《1042》是为庆祝乐队成立50周年之作，时长超过四十分钟，特邀Crucis贝斯手兼主唱Gustavo Montesano客串。乐评指出南美交响摇滚与欧美体系存在显著差异——同样宏大，却带着独特的内敛气质。整张专辑延续了乐队一贯的键盘主导路线，融入丰富的情绪转折和吉他独奏。

On 2 October it came back in two remixes on UK-based digital dub and reggae label Superchip: raggamuffin boom-bap from Hopebullet, a DJ and sound engineer from Osaka who also goes by Ranking Jin, and a second version by RJD. Behind it are deejay Daddy Cookiz and producer Simma, with singer Ponchita Peligros as guest. Simma is Nathan Simm from Hull, England, a producer and DJ who started out in Ableton during the 2020 lockdown, runs Superchip and also records as Polyecho and Square Nath. His 2024 debut, Simma Enters The Game, mixed digital reggae, dubbed-out hip-hop and 8-bit chiptune and drew on the German label Jahtari and the Scottish sound system Mungo’s Hi Fi. Daddy Cookiz has deejayed since 2005 and grew up on Jamaican sound system culture, and he takes his cues from Super Cat, Yellowman and Shabba Ranks. On the album he deejays in that rub-a-dub tradition over Simma’s digital sound, and Simma now takes that sound to Japan, where he performs with Hopebullet in Kyoto on 10 October, Tokyo on 19 October and Yokohama on 21 October, in a showcase for Superchip. Stream “Rub’a’Dub Love (Hopebullet Remix)” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Simma – Rub’a’Dub Love (Hopebullet Remix) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是英国赫尔制作人Simma（Nathan Simm）运营的独立厂牌Superchip发行的数字雷鬼混音作品。原曲收录于专辑《Where My Style Comes From》，由Deejay Daddy Cookiz在Simma制作的8-bit芯片音乐风格数字雷鬼伴奏上演绎，歌手Ponchita Peligros担任客串。此版Hopebullet混音由大阪DJ兼音响工程师Ranking Jin操刀，呈现raggamuffin boom-bap风格。Simma的首张专辑融合数字雷鬼、dub式嘻哈与8-bit芯片音乐，风格上受德国厂牌Jahtari及苏格兰声音系统Mungo's Hi Fi影响。Daddy Cookiz的唱词风格承袭Super Cat、Yellowman与Shabba Ranks等牙买加声音系统传统。Superchip作为英国独立小厂牌，体现了数字时代地下雷鬼场景与日本地下电子音乐圈的跨国联动。

items._cn_summary: Supereon 是一支来自挪威的三重奏，成员为贝斯手 Alexander Hoholm、钢琴家 Martin Gjede 与鼓手 Raymond Lavik，于 2024 年 8 月组建。《Phase I》是他们的首张专辑，延续了当代斯堪的纳维亚爵士乐那种不安分且具有探索性的精神内核。专辑并非让三件乐器各自独立陈述，而是试图在贝斯、钢琴与鼓的框架内构建一种开放、即兴驱动的对话关系。从钢琴三重奏的标准配置出发，乐队在即兴段落中寻找集体即兴的张力，节奏部分不再仅承担支撑功能，而是与和声乐器形成平等互动。整体气质介于自由爵士的解构冲动与现代爵士的旋律碎片之间，呈现出北欧爵士特有的冷峻质感与空间感。

items.body: New York-based musician Edley ODowd, formerly of Psychic TV, will release his second solo album, “Kowai-Yet,” on November 26, 2026 via the French label Arsenic Solaris. The ambient and experimental record follows his 2022 debut, “F(our)-Ward,” and arrives on vinyl and digital, with the Pink LP edition limited to 200 copies. ODowd recorded “Kowai-Yet” over three years in multiple locations. The album brings together material he made with collaborators he has worked with since leaving New York City to live closer to nature five years ago. The seven-track record shifts from the sound-collage approach of “F(our)-Ward” toward a more emotional register. “Where F(our)-Ward was more about sound collage, Kowai-Yet is about emotion,” ODowd says. “It’s infused with joy as well as a heaping dose of sadness.” The album’s title traces back to a single word. Describing a drive home on a summer night, ODowd recalls the sound of crickets against his car tires on humid pavement as both “sinister but compelling.” The Japanese word “kowai,” meaning “scary,” came to him first. At a stop sign, as the air went still, “quiet” followed, and the two merged into “Kowai-yet.” Individual tracks trace separate origins. “Heat” took shape through an improvised studio session in Los Angeles with engineer Joo Joo Ashworth, built from a drum pattern and expanded with analog electronics set against ODowd’s backwards saxophone. “Again” began as a more traditional song ODowd wrote alone. British musician Gore Tech later added a sharper beat, two guitarists contributed parts, and singer Zoah, whom ODowd met at a coffee shop along the Delaware River, added vocals and lyrics. “Arbiter” reworks stems ODowd had originally recorded for an unfinished song about his friend Lady Jaye Breyer P-Orridge. Its choruses use samples recorded during a 2000 trip to Nepal with Lady Jaye and Genesis P-Orridge, manipulated into the track. His Problem Addict collaborator Andrew Mann closes the song with guitar feedback. “Kowai-Yet” tracklist: 1. “Jamesey” 2. “Arbiter” 3. “Again” 4. “(Bruce Was) Kicked Out Of The Band” 5. “Heat” 6. “Sunrise” 7. “You’ll Never Know” Kowai-Yet release details “Kowai-Yet” is out November 26, 2026 via Arsenic Solaris as a digital album and a Pink LP limited to 200 copies. Both are available to pre-order on Bandcamp, where the track “Heat” is streaming now. Photo credits: Trevor Gregory. Kowai-Yet by Edley ODowd About Edley ODowd Edley ODowd grew up in the suburbs outside New York City and moved to Manhattan in the late 1980s, shortly after finishing high school. He got his start on a secondhand drum kit his mother bought him at a garage sale when he was 13. During a semester abroad in London in 1991, he joined the shoegaze band The Butterflies. Back in New York, he played drums and DJed for Toilet Boys, a band that wound down after a major European tour supporting the Red Hot Chili Peppers. In 2003, ODowd was instrumental in reviving Psychic TV, persuading Genesis P-Orridge to perform again. The reunited band’s first show took place at The Coral Room in New York City on December 5, 2003. ODowd founded the label Angry Love Productions after a self-funded Psychic TV EP sold out its 230 copies within two weeks. The “PTV3” lineup of Psychic TV played its final show on November 15, 2018. Alongside music, ODowd has worked as a graphic designer for major labels since 1993, taught courses at several universities in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and worked as a mental health counselor, including as a front-line worker during the COVID-19 pandemic. ODowd released his debut solo album, “F(our)-Ward,” as a self-released, ultra-limited cassette via Flesh Prison/DeathBed Tapes in 2022. Side-Line covered its expanded reissue, “F(our) ward,” released as a trifold-sleeved CD with three bonus tracks via the Italian label 13 on February 23, 2023. That same year, ODowd formed the death rock band Scorpion Tea with Christian Cruz, singer Anthony Diaz and bassist Fern Puma, signing to the label GIVE/TAKE. Side-Line covered the band’s debut single, “Scarlet Misquote,” in June 2023, ahead of the band’s self-titled debut album. ODowd now lives about an hour’s drive from New York City, where he continues to split his time between graphic design clients, band rehearsals and recording. “Kowai-Yet,” his second solo album, is set for release on November 26, 2026 via Arsenic Solaris.
items._cn_summary: 纽约音乐人Edley ODowd的第二张个人专辑即将由法国厂牌Arsenic Solaris发行。专辑以三年时间在多地录制完成，邀请多位合作者参与，包括洛杉矶录音师Joo Joo Ashworth、英国音乐人Gore Tech及歌手Zoah等。制作手法跨越即兴录音、模拟电子、反向萨克斯采样及人声拼贴，尤其在'Arbiter'一曲中使用了2000年尼泊尔旅行的田野录音素材。整张作品从首作的声响拼贴手法转向更情感化的表达，融合喜悦与忧伤的复杂情绪。专辑标题源自日语'可怕'与'安静'的结合，灵感来自夏夜驾车时蟋蟀声与潮湿路面的感官体验。Pink LP版本限量200张，体现了独立制作的小规模发行定位。

items.body: German-Finnish futurepop duo PLATRONiC will release the three-track EP “The Emperor’s New Clothes” on 16 October 2026, with three new takes on their March single “Fortress of Fools.” The song started with a poem written by Kay Burden, inspired by Hans Christian Andersen’s “The Emperor’s New Clothes.” Kay originally had a storytelling ballad in mind. Then Sami Jumppanen presented her with a considerably more danceable instrumental, and “Fortress of Fools” became something else entirely. PLATRONiC build three new versions of ‘Fortress of Fools’ For the new EP, they have gone back to the song and, appropriately enough, given it three new “dresses.” The first, “The Dark Electro Country Dress,” is a collaboration with On Moral Ends, the Linköping-based electronic project of Swedish songwriter, singer and multi-instrumentalist Andreas Svensson. His work moves through different electronic and alternative styles, making the collaboration a rather unusual match for PLATRONiC’s futurepop side. For “The Synthpop Mashup Dress,” PLATRONiC worked with Finnish keyboardist, producer and remixer Imppu from Lahti. His work stretches from danceable synthpop to more cinematic electronic sounds, and he has also created remixes and reworks for former Kraftwerk member Wolfgang Flür. The third version stays with Kay and Sami themselves: “The Dark Medieval Gothic Dress.” According to PLATRONiC, “Fortress of Fools” spent several weeks in the Top 10 of both the Klangwald Charts and GEWC following its release earlier this year. The track reached #8 in the Klangwald Charts. The video for “Fortress of Fools” was filmed in Savonlinna, Finland, and Alicante, Spain, and was created and produced by PLATRONiC. PLATRONiC formed in 2020 and consists of German singer-songwriter and co-producer Kay Burden and Finnish composer and producer Sami Jumppanen. Side-Line readers may also know the duo from “How To Ride The Wave,” which appeared earlier this year on Side-Line’s The Freya Files Ukraine benefit compilation. “The Emperor’s New Clothes” tracklist: 1. “Fortress of Fools – The Dark Electro Country Dress” (PLATRONiC & On Moral Ends) 2. “Fortress of Fools – The Synthpop Mashup Dress” (PLATRONiC & Imppu) 3. “Fortress of Fools – The Dark Medieval Gothic Dress” (PLATRONiC) Before the three new “dresses” arrive, “Fortress of Fools” already has its own visual counterpart. “The Emperor’s New Clothes” is available to pre-save via DistroKid ahead of its 16 October release. About PLATRONiC PLATRONiC released the single “Now!” in June 2022, followed by the EP “The Healing” in April 2023 and a cover of Depeche Mode’s “The Things You Said” that August. A reworked version of their debut single “Pride” followed in June 2024, then the winter single “Winter Stores” that December. In March 2025, they released the teaser video for “How to Ride the Wave,” and in December 2025 contributed a cover of Depeche Mode’s “But Not Tonight” to the “In Your Memory 2” tribute compilation. “Fortress of Fools” followed in March 2026 as the duo’s most recent original single, ahead of “The Emperor’s New Clothes” EP arriving on 16 October.
items._cn_summary: 德芬二人组合PLATRONiC以安徒生童话《皇帝的新衣》为灵感，创作单曲《Fortress of Fools》，并在此EP中为该曲编织三套全新"外衣"。首版与瑞典电子项目On Moral Ends合作，呈现暗电子乡村风格；其次邀请芬兰键盘手Imppu打造合成器流行混搭版本；最后由二人亲自操刀的暗中世纪哥特版收尾。歌曲最初源于Kay Burden撰写的诗作，后经Sami Jumppanen的舞曲化编曲彻底转变形态。该曲曾在Klangwald和GEWC榜单打入前十。MV拍摄于芬兰萨翁林纳与西班牙阿利坎特。整体企划概念有趣，三种迥异风格的重塑展现了一定的跨界实验意识，但作为futurepop基底作品，创新深度有限，更偏向类型内部的常规混搭探索。

items.body: Berkeley, California spoken word industrial artist Ms Xxan released the two-track single shaper of decrepitude. on October 5, 2026, through her own Bandcamp page. The single pairs its title track with “ghosted.” and follows her spoken word dark ambient album “Make Yourself the Lie” by less than a month. Ms Xxan wrote, performed, composed and produced both tracks herself. The release pairs spoken-word vocals with doom-paced, noise-industrial production in the death-industrial and harsh-noise register that runs through her catalogue. She flags the single with a content warning for lyrics that may affect mental health sensitivities. shaper of decrepitude. by Ms Xxan “shaper of decrepitude.” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp. About Ms Xxan Ms Xxan writes, performs and produces spoken word and industrial noise music from Berkeley, California. She released the nine-track spoken word dark ambient album “Make Yourself the Lie” on September 8, 2026, as a free, name-your-price download via VūMantra Records, the Berlin label founded in 2019 by Vince Gagliardi, who also records as The Nent and LAGÁN. That album carried a content warning for explicit lyrics addressing depression, and the same material also circulates as a podcast on Apple Podcasts and Audiomack. Ms Xxan handles writing, performance, composition and production on her own across both releases. With “shaper of decrepitude.”, she returned to self-releasing directly on Bandcamp, pairing the title track with “ghosted.” as a quick follow-up to the VūMantra album.
items._genre: spoken word / dark ambient / industrial / noise
items._cn_summary: 加州伯克利的口语艺术与工业噪音音乐人Ms Xxan于2026年10月通过Bandcamp自行发行了两首单曲合集《shaper of decrepitude.》，距离她在柏林厂牌VūMantra Records发行的九曲专辑《Make Yourself the Lie》不到一个月。该合集由她自己独立完成词曲、表演、作曲与制作工作，标题曲与"ghosted."并置，口语人声与末日节奏的噪音工业制作相结合，呈现出死亡工业与极端噪音的色彩。整张作品延续了她此前专辑中以口语诗为主轴、辅以黑暗氛围音景的手法，歌词涉及抑郁等心理健康议题，因此附带内容警告。同名作品作为数字单曲在Bandcamp上架后，她回归了直接自发行的方式，作为厂牌专辑的快速后续。从音乐定位看，口语艺术与工业噪音的融合具有一定的实验属性，但文章更偏向新闻稿性质，对声音设计细节与艺术意图的阐述较为有限。

items.body: 『声なき声のドローイング:スキャン画像』2026［© Shu Yonezawa, Courtesy of SNOW Contemporary］ 会期：2026/07/17～2026/09/05 会場：SNOW Contemporary［東京都］ 公式サイト：http://snowcontemporary.com/exhibition/202607.html 「声なき声のキャラクター」は米澤柊による個展である。展示作品はすべて2026年の新作で、なかでも米澤がここ一年ほど取り組んでいるという油絵作品が全体の七割近くを占めている。画面はどれも彩度の低い色が細かく重ねられることで構成されており、その茫洋とした色彩の渦を眺めるうちに、人間めいた輪郭や骨格、目、手の残像といったものたちの印象がかろうじて浮かび上がってくる。これは直感的には、白飛びした視界を思わせた。眠りから醒めたときに誰しもが味わうように、暗がりから急に光に満ちた空間へと晒された視界は明順応が間に合わず白く飽和する。そしてそこから徐々に、事物の輪郭や色彩を取り戻していく。しかし本展において、その視界が完全に明瞭になることはない。作品のあいだを行き交うにしたがい、眼球を包む涙液そのものが白濁していくかのごとく、乳白色の闇がゆるやかに立ち込める。六本木の雑居ビルの薄暗がりを切り開いてあらわれる端正なホワイトキューブともあいまって、本展はどこまでも明るく、しかし──それゆえに──知覚の不完全性を露わにしている。では、そんな淡い光の中に漂っているものたちとは一体なんなのだろうか。 ［撮影：木奥惠三］ 繰り返し述べられてきた内容のため簡潔に触れるにとどめるが、多くの手法やメディウムを横断した米澤の制作には「アニマ（魂・生命性）」への関心が通底しており、とりわけ特徴的なのが「オバケ」への着目である。「オバケ」とはアニメーション制作において、あるフレームとフレームのあいだの動きを補完し、物体の動きをより活き活きとみせるためにあえて（静止画としては）崩れた描写を行なう技術を指す。実際、現時点における米澤作品のもっとも一般的なイメージとは、身体がほどけて散らばりつつあるかのような「オバケ」としてのキャラクターたちの図像だろう。 画面内の事物を 息づかせ （ アニメートす ） るための技術が「オバケ」と呼ばれる逆説──いや、考えてみれば逆説ではないのだ。さまざまなアニメ作品において、「オバケ」のコマを単体で切り取ったスクリーンショットは作画崩壊の事例としてネットミーム化してきた。これはアニメーションの中割り技術への無知から生じた誤認にすぎないわけだが、ではなぜ人々が「オバケ」に対してそれほど強烈な印象を共有しえたのかといえば、なめらかなアニメーションのなかに「見てはいけないものを見てしまった」と感じたからにほかならないだろう。すなわち、「オバケ」とはアニメーションの物語時間を補填するために見逃され続けることを運命付けられた存在であり、それゆえ、ひとたび意識に上ったその姿は本物の怪異さながらに「ぞっとする」ものとなるのだ。 画面内におけるキャラクターの自律性が担保されるためには、無数の崩れかけた非-自律的な なにものか ・・・・・ が不可欠であるというジレンマ。米澤はこの主従──アニメーションを規定する所与の時間と、それを埋め合わせる「オバケ」という関係性──を撹乱する。ほんらい見てはいけないものである「オバケ」を一枚の図像──しかもモニタやキャンバスといったいかにも「見るべき」質感を帯びたもの──として固定したうえで、その身体の崩壊を過剰に押し進めていく。そのとき、アニメーションのなめらかさを整えるパテのごとき不定形な「オバケ」はフレームの隙間から這い出して、別の時間的秩序を育み始める──フレームレートに従って生起する単線的な物語とは異なる時間を。そこでは過去や未来は等しくまなざされ、因果もまた意味を失う。米澤はそうして、フレームとフレームのあいだの飛躍を補完するためにのみ生を許された存在に、 別種の生の可能性 （ アニマ ） を見ようとするわけだ。 このようにアニメーションをひとつの基点とする米澤の作品群は、その手法にかかわらず複雑な層性を帯びてきた。例えば米澤の代表的なシリーズである「オバケのスクリーンショット」では、現実の風景写真のなかに「オバケ」としてのキャラクターたちが描き込まれている。レイヤーの集合としてのデジタルペイントが現実の風景に重ね合わされ、しかもそれは連続する無数のフレームの一瞬を捉えた「スクリーンショット」として位置付けられる。こうした時間的・空間的な複層性のなかをたゆたう米澤の作品は、必然的に「いま・ここ」からの遊離を予感させる。イメージは確かに目の前に存在するはずなのに、どこかヴェールに包まれているような捉えどころのなさがついてまわる。それは失われたものへの憧憬なのか、来たるべきものの予兆なのか──無論、どちらでもありうる。先に述べたとおり、米澤が紡ごうとする非線形の時間的秩序のなかにおいて、過去・現在・未来は等価に立ち並んでいるのだから★1。アニマはつねに、現前と予感のあいだで見え隠れする。 この観点において、描画面をレイヤー状に切り分けるためのアナログな技術として油絵を位置付けることも可能だろう。しかし当然ながら、油絵においては絵具の乾燥状態が層を決定する。乾ききる前に次のストロークを置けば下の層は物理的に巻き込まれ、層と層の境界——それは時間的秩序そのものと言ってもいい——が相互に浸潤可能となる（もちろん、実際に米澤がそのような描法を用いたかどうかは問題ではない）。ここで層を決定しているのは描き手の意志ではなく、絵具の乾燥速度、すなわちメディウムに固有の時間である。フレームとフレームを繋ぐフラットな時間のあいだから、「オバケ」が棲まう異なる時間が這い出していったように、ここでは層と層のあいだにメディウム由来の液体的な時間感覚が流れ込んでいる★2。 ［撮影：斉藤桃加］ 本展のステートメント冒頭には「かたちを選んで描こうとするほど選ばなかったものを切りすててしまうようで息苦しく、絵は段々と白くなっていった」とある。幾重にもゆらぎながら仄かに浮かび上がる油彩のイメージは、さまざまな連想を喚起する。例えば長時間露光による写真。そこでは被写体が動くことによって輪郭がブレ、イメージは次第に発散へと向かっていく。あるいは拡散モデルにおける画像生成（を開始まもなく停止させたようす）。ここでは反対に、ブレの極点とでもいうべきノイズのなかに任意の輪郭が幻視され、イメージが浮かび上がってくる。輪郭が浮かび上がる前のさざめきと、輪郭が溶け去っていった後の残響。米澤の画面が置かれているのは、まさにその異なる二つのベクトルが調停され、判定が無化される地点／時点である。 米澤は「世界が意味になる前の複雑さについて考えたい」という。しかしここまで見てきたように「ほんらいの複雑な世界が、人間の手による記号的分節によって単純化されてしまう」という単線的な因果とは別の場所に向けてこそ、米澤の作品はひらかれているように思える。そういえば、私が米澤の油絵の画面からはじめに想起したもの。それは写真でもAIでもなく、ほとんど面影だけになってしまった記憶のことであった。限界まで薄れ抽象化された記憶は、それがどこに属するのかをもはや判別できず、ゆえに時間のあいだを自由に飛び回り、私たちの認識に影響を及ぼして回る。はじめて見たはずのものをなぜか懐かしく思うこと。反対に、何度も見たはずのものをなぜだか瑞々しく感じること。そうした認識の脱臼ともいうべき瞬間を真に受けて生き続けることが、可能であるように思えるのだ。米澤の作品世界においてならば。 ★1──個人的にここで想起するのは小林泰三「酔歩する男」である。作中では、一風変わったタイムトラベルの方法が描かれる。登場人物は「時間とは本来非連続なものであり、そこに連続性を見出しているのは私たちの脳である」との仮説を示し、実際に脳内の時間感覚を司る部位を破壊することで、さまざまな時間点をランダムに飛び回る存在となる。それは過去と未来が等しく可能性のなかに溶け込んだ非線形の人生であり、そこには始まりも終わりもありえない。 ★2──ここで思い出すのは、ジェフ・ウォールによるエッセイ「Photography and Liquid Intelligence」（1989）である。ウォールは、写真を織りなす光学と液体の緊張関係に焦点を当てた。つまりカメラという緻密な機械が生産する写真は、最終的に現像という液体の不確定性に晒されることで顕現するのであり、ウォールはここに乾いた近代的知性のオルタナティブとしての湿った知性、液体的知性を見るのである。エッセイはこの液体的知性をソラリスの海に喩えることで結ばれる。観測者の記憶からイメージを汲み出し反射させるその海には、結ばれる前のあらゆるイメージの素がたゆたいながら、こちらを見返しているわけだ。写真とは、現像液に潜む無数のイメージのひとつをたまさか拾い上げたものにすぎず、もう一度現像し直せばそこにはまったく違ったイメージが掬い取られるのかもしれない。フィルムを現像液に浸し続ければ、その還元力はやがて感光していない臭化銀にまで至り、あらゆるイメージを黒く塗りつぶしていく。それは白く飽和した油彩のイメージと対になるものだろう。 （後編へ） 鑑賞日：2026/07/25（土）

items._cn_summary: 文章实为米澤柊個展的評論，而非音樂專輯。展覽以動畫「幀間」為核心，將原本服務於敘事連續性的崩解形象「オバケ」固定為油彩與數位繪畫中可觀看的圖像，探討角色自律性、非線性時間與媒介自身的時間性。評論把油彩乾燥形成的層次浸潤、長曝光攝影的輪廓模糊與生成圖像的雜訊並置，描述一種尚未分化出明確形體、仍保有生長可能性的知覺狀態。內容具備前衛藝術的理論密度，但並非音樂。

items.body: Trippin’ is timely, the London (Ontario) label cementing the Newfoundland-based producer’s growing profile with a more substantial presence. A rollout spanning a couple of years via teaser and remix releases Trippin' by Zachary Gray   Canadian ambient/electronic practitioner Zachary Gray’s album Trippin’ is set to land on A Person Disguised as People. The 9-track LP comes on the back of the previous Suburbia EP (APDAP, 2024) (see igloo’view) with a rollout spanning a couple of years via teaser and remix releases. Nov. 2024 saw a 2-track taster Trippin’ / In Arrears (igloo’view here) as part of APDAP‘s A/B Series; back then the title track tasted like a ‘a doleful brooder, replete with melodic synth lines recalling early 90s Warp luminaries (cf. Black Dog, Plaid), layers of rhythm and harmony making for an uneasy introspective tenor’ (igloo’view), with ‘a deft touch in blending electronic production detail and filmic affect’ overall commended. Spin-off EP Trippin’ Variations (igloo’view here) followed Feb. 2025, featuring re-thinks of the title track by mates of Gray incl. Hidden Rivers, SXXN, Soft Operator and James Scott. Now comes the full release, somewhat later than planned—Autumn 2026; the Fall that pride came before perhaps! The album furthers the evolution of Gray’s anatomy, tracing years of his musical composition, revision and memory, from a back catalog grounded in early releases such as Under a Red Sky (Synesthesia Media, 2020), Plan B (APDAP, 2020), Hustle Movement (APDAP, 2017), Night Hustle (APDAP, 2016), Containment (APDAP, 2015) plus collabs with luminaries like Benoît Pioulard, Montag, and Sea Oleena. Trippin’ is timely, the London (Ontario) label cementing the Newfoundland-based producer’s growing profile with a more substantial presence. Trippin’ is out on Oct. 9 on A Person Disguised as People. [Bandcamp] Trippin' by Zachary Gray   The post Zachary Gray :: Trippin’ (A Person Disguised as People) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自加拿大纽芬兰的电子/环境音乐制作人Zachary Gray，由伦敦（安大略）的独立厂牌A Person Disguised as People发行，是其多年创作的阶段性总结。专辑为9首曲目，延续了此前EP《Suburbia》的脉络，融合了环境电子与IDM元素，合成器旋律线让人联想到早期90年代Warp厂牌的Black Dog、Plaid等艺人。制作上注重电子制作细节与影像化情感氛围的结合，节奏与和声层层叠加，营造出内省而略显不安的情绪基调。专辑经过数年通过单曲、混音EP等形式逐步铺垫推出，体现出独立厂牌对艺术家长期项目的支持。整体而言，这是一张延续Warp系美学的氛围电子作品，适合偏好低调、沉思类电子聆听的听众。

items._cn_summary: 意大利电子音乐人 Lorenzo Senni 六年磨一剑，回归 Warp 厂牌发行新专辑《All Ages》。这张收录十一首曲目的唱片是他首次大量使用人声的作品，合作者包括 Xiu Xiu 主唱 Jamie Stewart 以及滑板选手 Chad Muska 与 Jamie Thomas。专辑延续了其标志性的失重感 Trance 声响，同时注入硬核朋克的精神内核——标题即指硬核演出中人人可入的开放态度。Senni 自述曾以直边少年身份混迹于嗑药锐舞派对，这种边缘身份交融也贯穿于专辑之中，将锐舞的高能与硬核的态度编织在一起。整体作品在 Trance 的绵长循环与朋克的爆发力之间寻找平衡，展现出独立电子艺术家罕见的跨界视野。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Released in 2001, 'Bridge Across Forever' is the second album by progressive rock supergroup Transatlantic. Featuring members of prog heavyweights Dream Theater, Spock's Beard, Marillion and The Flower Kings, this album comes out just one year after the release of their debut, and despite all still maintaining positions in the own respective, fulltime bands, there is a very palpable and effortless chemistry between everyone involved. With four songs totalling at almost one hour and 20 minutes of music, this is an ambitious project, and will indeed take multiple listens to familiarise yourself with it all. There are so many twists and turns, every track is a journey through various musical ideas and themes, that it's just a matter of putting in the time. As you'd expect with musicians of this calibre, the performances and writing are of a high standard, and all four men doubling up on vocal duties keeps the songs sounding fresh and interesting. With particular highlights including tracks such as 'Duel With the Devil' and 'Stranger in Your Soul', 'Bridge Across Forever' is a worthy addition to any prog collection, and firmly establishes Transatlantic as more than just another side-project.
items._cn_summary: Transatlantic是由Dream Theater、Spock's Beard、Marillion及The Flower Kings成员组成的跨团超级计划，《Bridge Across Forever》是其2001年发行的第二张专辑，仅以四首曲目承载近八十分钟的庞大篇幅。乐评指出乐队成员尽管各自仍有全职乐队，却在此展现出极为自然且默契的化学反应。整张专辑充满频繁的主题转换与乐段转折，每首歌都是一段跨越多种音乐观念的旅程，需要反复聆听才能完全消化。人声由四位成员轮替分担，使作品的音色层次保持新鲜感。评论特别提及《Duel With the Devil》与《Stranger in Your Soul》作为亮点曲目，认为此作足以证明Transatlantic并非单纯的副业项目，而是具备独立价值的创作实体。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "For the Love of Art and the Making" is the third full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act Beyond Twilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works ofanother band). The album was released through Massacre Records in April 2006. It�s the successor to"Section X" from March 2005. There has been one lineup change since "Section X" as lead vocalistKelly Sundown Carpenter has been replaced by Swedish singer Bj�rn Jansson."For the Love of Art and the Making" is quite an interesting release as it�s basically one, 37:49minutes long composition broken down into 43 sub tracks. Stylistically it�s a continuation of thepower/progressive metal style of the preceding releases and as Jansson is a suitable and not toodifferent sounding replacement for Carpenter, the change on the lead vocalist spot doesn�t changemuch in terms of consistency of the band�s sound. The many short sub tracks makes "For the Love ofArt and the Making" a very different listening experience though as the tracks form only short partsof a longer track, they don�t have much time to evolve.It�s not that this is simple or one-dimensional music, because the tracks often shift in dynamicsbetween a heavy power/progressive metal oriented approach and more subtle and mellow parts. A normalverse/chorus structured composition wouldn�t work that way because it�s longer and you have time todevelop ideas over the course of a longer playing time. Here the short track lengths mean that ideasare executed fast and they flow by even faster. I�m not sure I think it always work that well,because sometimes I feel Beyond Twilight could have done a lot more with some of the parts, but atthat point they have usually already moved on to the next section. So, although "For the Love of Art and the Making" is a both well produced and well performedrelease, the songwriting approach will probably divide the waters. There�s arguably a lot of qualityhere but as an album I�m not sure I think "For the Love of Art and the Making" works that well. Tomy ears it�s more a study in interesting ideas and high level musicianship. Thinking of "For theLove of Art and the Making" as a single coherent composition doesn�t cross my mind while listeningto the album. The song is constantly disrupted and changes gears and dynamics and it�s actually abit stressful to listen to. When that is said "For the Love of Art and the Making" is still a highquality release, but I�m pretty sure it�s an acquired taste, so enter at your own risk. A 3.5 star(70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦前卫力量金属乐队Beyond Twilight的第三张录音室专辑，整张专辑被构建为单一37分49秒的连贯作品，分解为43个短小段落。新主唱Björn Jansson接替Kelly Sundown Carpenter，音色过渡自然。音乐在重金属段落与柔和抒情段之间频繁切换动力与情绪，构思快速且密集，乐手技术水准较高，制作精良。然而短小的段落结构导致想法来不及展开即被切断，整体缺乏完整的作品凝聚力，听感上更像是高水平的片段化构思集合而非有机统一的整体。这种碎片化的写作手法使专辑呈现出实验性的结构探索，但同时也牺牲了旋律的呼吸感与情绪的持续积累，最终成为一份需要特定审美倾向才能欣赏的分裂性作品。

Redemption belongs to the group of bands that emerged under that inspiring influence, shaping a powerful and virtuosic musical approach, immersed in the intricate
items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — The progressive metal movement, whose foundations were first laid in the mid-to-late 1980s by pioneers such as Queensr�che, Fates Warning, and Dream Theater, gained a much stronger identity and momentum during the 1990s, eventually expanding and establishing itself as a fully-fledged genre in the 2000s. Redemption belongs to the group of bands that emerged under that inspiring influence, shaping a powerful and virtuosic musical approach, immersed in the intricate structures of the most contemporary prog metal.With their self-titled 2003 debut album, Redemption had already shown what they were capable of, although it was still a somewhat raw and unpolished power-metal-style offering with nascent progressive elements. For "The Fullness of Time" (2005), their second album, the band led by Nick van Dyk brought in the duo James Sherwood (bass) and Chris Quirarte (drums), both from the ranks of the Los Angeles-based band Prymary, as their new rhythm section, and, most importantly, vocalist Ray Alder -who also fronted Fates Warning- evolving toward a more defined and mature sound.The first third of the album retains the band's seminal sound, with machine-gun-like, galloping riffs; frenzied, counterpointing solos between Bernie Versailles and van Dyk; and Quirarte's wild double-bass drumming, to which van Dyk's keyboards add an additional, fitting melodic and atmospheric layer, both on the aggressive "Threads," the fast-paced "Scarred," and the reflective and bitter "Parker's Eyes" -which offers a somber and disheartening view of the world, including a reference to the events of 9/11- and incorporates a beautiful, arpeggiated acoustic nuance before exploding instrumentally.The following two-thirds reflect the band's solidity and progressive character, with the epic "Sapphire", a powerful and expansive instrumental tapestry led by a spirited Alder on vocals and generous with guitar and synthesizer solos, contrasted with calm, refreshing passages -the jewel of the album- and the intricate "The Fullness of Time," a suite divided into four sections where journeys through rocky peaks -the furious and vengeful "i. Rage" and the resilient "iii. Release"- alternate with clear, evocative sonic valleys -the meditative "ii. Despair" and the hopeful and luminous "iv. Trascendence"."The Fullness of Time" marked a turning point in Redemption's career: an album in which the band left behind the rough edges of its debut to find its own identity, delivering one of the genre's strongest offerings of the mid-2000s.4/4.5 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / melodic metal
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是前卫金属乐队Redemption的第二张全长作品，乐队以Nick van Dyk为核心键盘/吉他手，引入Fates Warning主唱Ray Alder及洛杉矶Prymary乐队的节奏组，完成了从粗糙首作向成熟之声的过渡。前三分之一延续乐队初期风格，以急促切分节奏、双底鼓驱动和双吉他对位独奏为核心，键盘铺设旋律与氛围层。后三分之二展现乐队的成熟与前卫特质，四乐章套曲在全曲中以愤怒与绝望的山谷与希望超脱的高地交替铺陈，形成完整的叙事弧线。专辑整体仍属于主流前卫金属范畴，在技术层面有较高完成度，但在声音设计或跨界实验方面没有显著突破。

items.body: Montreal dark-alternative artist Martin Saint released the single “Endless Bridge” on October 6, 2026, as a standalone digital track on Bandcamp. Martin Saint wrote and arranged “Endless Bridge” himself and handled vocals and guitars. Julie Abel plays piano, Frank Bones plays drums and Jack Vignavong plays bass. The track was recorded at Martini Lounge, Indica Studio 24 and Studio Pacifique in Montreal by Frank Bones and Martin Saint, with assistance from Olivier René de Cotret. Frank Bones mixed and mastered the track and co-produced it with Martin Saint. Ursa Minor handled the sleeve photography and design. Endless Bridge by Martin Saint In the track’s Bandcamp notes, Martin Saint described the song as a love story told through departures and returns. “Endless Bridge is about as close to a love song as I’ll ever get, but there’s a bittersweetness to it. Beginnings, endings, renewals. It expresses faith in the future and letting go of forces holding us back, even if this may take a lifetime.” He pointed to two specific reference points for the track’s sound: “Musically, I wanted something that’d sound as epic as The Killing Moon or With or Without You, for example. Melancholy, foggy, but uplifting and catchy.” “Endless Bridge” is available now as a name-your-price digital download on Bandcamp, with a minimum price of $1.50. About Martin Saint Martin Saint is a solo artist based in Montreal, Québec. Before launching the project under his own name, he was the lead singer and second guitarist of the city’s indie-rock quartet The Ember Glows, active between 2019 and 2024. His solo material moves into darker, more atmospheric territory, with baritone, emotionally-charged vocals and poetic lyrics that he has linked to Bauhaus, The Mission, The Jesus and Mary Chain, Nick Cave, Leonard Cohen and The Doors. “Endless Bridge” follows “Seekers,” Martin Saint’s fifth release under the solo name, out April 18, 2025. The ten-track album was recorded and mixed in Montreal at the Martini Lounge and Orange Studio by Martin Saint and Frank Bones, who also mastered it, with guest contributions from Julie Abel on piano, Delphine Dupont on lead guitar and backing vocals, Kevin Hills on bass, Hugo Joyal on pedal steel and Ursa Minor on backing vocals and artwork. His catalog also includes the albums “One Word Away,” “Fly Tales” and “Radio Murmurs,” along with the singles “Last Lights,” “The Law” and “I’ll Be Your Stranger,” featuring Ursa Minor. “Endless Bridge” carries the same core production team as “Seekers” into a new standalone single.
items._cn_summary: 蒙特利尔独立音乐人 Martin Saint 发行单曲《Endless Bridge》，延续其从乐队 The Ember Glows 转型后的暗色调另类风格。歌曲由 Saint 本人创作并担任主唱与吉他手，联合键盘、鼓、贝斯手共同录制于蒙特利尔多家工作室。Saint 将其描述为一首带有苦涩感的爱情歌，主题围绕离别与重逢、放手与对未来的信念展开。音乐上他以 The Killing Moon、With or Without You 为参照，追求忧郁朦胧但兼具史诗感与悦耳度的氛围。作品以男中音情感化的演唱与诗意歌词为核心，融合后朋克、哥特摇滚与另类民谣元素，在自主发行框架下保持完整的制作团队协作。作为独立单曲发布于 Bandcamp，这首歌延续了他此前全长专辑《Seekers》的制作班底，结构工整但创新性有限。

items.body: Everything and Nothing The consistently excellent Hammock are back with Everything and Nothing. For Hammock, Everything and Nothing is an album that spreads its hands wide to encompass two beautiful extremes. They push the music to the limits – and past the limits – of where it’s gone before. Glowing guitars, their crisp-but-blurred notes floating in the breeze, link arms with a gorgeous, inspiring set of vocals, but this time a driving, propulsive percussion, strong enough to be different, is introduced to the mix, giving the music even more of an ethereal edge that borders the mouth-watering shores of shoegaze without ever sacrificing or losing its cinematic ambient / post-rock feeling that has, since the beginning, defined their music. On ‘Clarity’, the guitars are a bit rougher, a bit grittier and a little more substantial, which in turn lends the music more energy. It’s just as if the reclined music’s suddenly downed a large glass of Lucozade. ‘Glassy Blue’ slows things down, its structure like that of an ambient pop song with its repeating, ghostly chorus and its shimmering melodic lines contributing to the haze. And a lot of the tracks do come across as having a definite ABAB form, or, failing that, a repeating chorus. The track is the bright blue of the summer sky, open and inviting. The reverb simultaneously smears and softens the music, acting as a windbreaker against Everything and Nothing’s stronger currents of air. The wet reverb is more like a pool than a puddle. And there are softer, more introspective moments that arrive as soon as the piano on ‘Marathon Boy’ starts to play. Hammock’s music always has a scent for the bigger things in life – they hint at wider things beyond our current level of understanding or comprehension, of the stars in the night sky and the galaxies swirling over our heads. Their music glows with a shy sense of spectacle, a quiet, unfolding drama made all the more powerful in a world that shouts for attention. Special memories and cherished moments blend in with more colourful, sugary highs this time around. Unexpectedly, there are elements of shoegaze inside, but the sweeping, air-cleansing instrumental sound still lies at the heart of the music. The pedalboards are immense and as wide as a blue sky absent of clouds, the volume swelling and then swirling in an ephemeral soundscape that has the capability to chug at the same time. But on ‘Wasted We Stared at the Ceiling’, softer curves enter the music, the vocals wrapped up in seductive layers of delay and distortion. Carefree, blissed-out memories, bleary Saturday mornings and after-school parties are reminisced through the music, but it’s also a reflection on a period that can never be repeated. There’s also something of the present moment in their music, of just being. It’s mindfulness in music. Nothing else matters, because with the flutter of an eyelid a single moment fades away and a new one begins. That’s all there ever has been, and that’s all there ever will be. ‘We Were So Young’ is a celebratory anthem of youth and friendship, sparkling effervescently with a liberal amount of energy as its louder music rocks out. It’s the sound of freedom itself, of the sun never setting. The silky feminine vocals float through the air with a beautiful transparency, the very being of the music glowing in the light of the sun. ‘Unspoken’ and ‘Before You Float Away Into Nothing’ tail the music off. As if carried on the two wings of a bird, the music flies away. Regarding the genre tag, it doesn’t really matter. The sound is immense – Everything and Nothing is probably their best release to date, and that’s saying something. They’ll take your breath away again. www.shop.hammockmusic.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了乐队一贯的电影感氛围路线，吉他音色在清亮与模糊之间游走，加入了更具推进力的鼓点，使整体边缘向shoegaze靠拢，但未牺牲其环境音与后摇的内核。湿漉漉的混响像水面一样包裹住旋律，人声被延迟与失真层层包裹，营造出冥想式的氛围。编曲上多首曲目呈现ABAB结构与重复副歌，从明亮开放到内省柔软均有覆盖，钢琴段落提供了更私密的情感空间。整体音乐带有一种安静的戏剧感，在喧嚣世界中以低姿态呈现辽阔意象，融合了记忆中的无忧时光与当下正念的感知。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: Sean Cooney 以1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场屠杀（Peterloo惨案）为题材创作了一张原创民谣专辑，将历史事件转化为歌曲叙事。专辑以书籍形式呈现，收录当时的信件、政治漫画和插图，构成多媒体作品。音乐上邀请了Eliza Carthy（小提琴/演唱）、Sam Carter（吉他）、Ben Nicholls（多乐器）和Lancashire工业民谣歌手Jennifer Reid（旁白）参与。歌曲结构上捕捉了集会当日的期待、军队冲击时的恐惧与悲恸，既关注Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等普通人的故事，也通过《Monkey Rides The Mare》三段式刻画士兵的傲慢。三位歌手的声线构成强有力的三重组合。整体定位为具有社会关怀的历史民谣，面向对工人阶级历史题材感兴趣的听众。
