items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary sound art
items._cn_summary: 这是一张基于芝加哥南区街头录音的声音作品，二十五位枪支暴力亲历者在前廊上讲述自身经历，录音地点位于中洛米德机场降落航线下方，蚊子声与街头环境音构成背景层。制作者Ian Brennan强调未添加任何音乐，所有声音均来自现场。文章并非传统乐评，而是编者按形式呈现录音背后的社会语境，包括参与者年龄跨度从十七岁到六十七岁、一位老人讲述失去两个儿子的经历。收益将捐给Cure Violence Global。作为田野录音与声音艺术的结合，作品具有强烈的纪实性与社会议题色彩，但对偏好实验音乐与声音设计的听众而言，其音乐性较弱，更偏向社论性质的内容载体。

Captured during a performance at Reykjavík's Harpa Concert Hall on 24 October 2021, the show saw Björk play music mostly from 2004 album Medúlla. For the performance, she was joined by the 50-member Hamrahlíð Choir, who were conducted by Þorgerður Ingólfsdóttir. Musician Bergur Þórisson also provided accompaniment on the organ. The album will be released across vinyl, CD, DVD and Blu-ray formats, and features renditions of 11 of Björk's tracks. In a statement, the Icelandic artist said: "I am so happy and proud of this concert.... items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Auto Reconnaissance' is the kind of prog album you would play if you're already a fan of TheTangent (or any contemporary symphonic/retro prog band playing this kind of music), and that'sperfectly fine because every new release from the Andy Tillison-led band is a real treat. I cannotcomprehend how he has been able to come up with so many great albums, and while this particular oneis one of the most laid-back, charming, and "conventional" Tangent albums, it is still packed withsome excellent tunes and brilliant playing.The lineup here consists of drummer Steve Roberts, guitarist Luke Machine, bassist Jonas Reingold,and sax player Theo Travis, and I have the impression that this is one of the longest-lastinglineups in the history of the band, responsible for a couple of really fine records under TheTangent name.Anyway, 'Auto Reconnaissance' continues the distinctive blend of melodic retro prog and groovy jazz-rock and does not differ dramatically from its predecessors. In fact, I feel like this is one of theleast experimental albums from the group, which is nevertheless compensated for by the fineproduction and overall relaxing atmosphere of the album. Two long-form pieces appear, and in-betweenthem four standard-length tracks give us glimpses of the different musical personalities of AndyTillison. Upbeat opener 'Life on Hold' is a song I am quite keen on, probably because of its gushysynths and groove-heavy rhythm. This is followed by the nearly 16-minute-long travel log suite'Jinxed in Jersey', which is an interesting surprise and one of my favorite tracks on the album.Apart from Tillison's curious narration (of his journey in Jersey), it also covers a wide array ofstyles in a brilliant manner. The other really fun track here is 'The Tower of Babel', which is morethan I can say for the 28-minute opus 'Lie Back & Think of England'.I have listened to this piece several times and I still do not find anything exceptional or excitingabout it. It seems to be a meandering epic that explores a sequence of disparate ideas, leaving mostof them underdeveloped in the context of the whole piece. The bonus track 'Proxima' is reallyenjoyable, blending together Tillison's progressive electronic soundscapes with the jazzy playing ofhis bandmates. All in all, 'Auto Reconnaissance' by The Tangent is a really good and relaxing albumthat feels too safe to be recognized as one of their all-time best.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了乐队标志性的复古前卫摇滚与爵士摇滚融合路线，键盘主导的旋律编排与萨克斯交织，形成轻松愉悦的整体氛围。专辑包含两首长篇作品和四首标准长度曲目，开场曲以合成器与律动节奏打底，十六分钟的旅行日志式组曲在叙事中展现多样风格转换，末段二十八分钟的大型作品则因想法过于发散而显得缺乏凝聚力。从制作角度看，录音品质精良，乐手演奏水准出色，但整体风格偏向保守与传统，在实验性探索方面着墨有限。乐评认为这是一张舒适耐听的专辑，但对熟悉乐队作品的老听众而言缺乏足够的惊喜与突破。

items.album: David J releases ‘Requiem for the Rose Garden’, first single from new album ‘Postcards from the Afterlife’
items.excerpt: David J, a co-founder, bassist and co-songwriter of the post-punk bands Bauhaus and Love and Rockets, releases the single “Requiem for the Rose Garden” on 51 Recordings on 8 October 2026. The song is a protest aimed at the Trump administration, built around the White House Rose Garden as a target that is both symbolic and literal. It is the first track confirmed from J’s new album “Postcards from the Afterlife,” due 27 November on double LP, CD and digital formats.
items.body: David J, a co-founder, bassist and co-songwriter of the post-punk bands Bauhaus and Love and Rockets, releases the single “Requiem for the Rose Garden” on 51 Recordings on 8 October 2026. The song is a protest aimed at the Trump administration, built around the White House Rose Garden as a target that is both symbolic and literal. It is the first track confirmed from J’s new album “Postcards from the Afterlife,” due 27 November on double LP, CD and digital formats. David J on ‘Requiem for the Rose Garden’ J points to physical changes made at the White House since Donald Trump’s first term in office when he explains the song. “It’s basically a protest about Trump’s administration and the atrocities it has visited upon the USA,” he said. “In the context of the song, the Rose Garden at the White House can be seen as a symbolic metaphor, although it is also quite literal. I actually wrote it during Trump’s first term in office when he had that beautiful garden hacked up. Now, even more horror has been inflicted on it of course, and the elegant East Wing of the building completely decimated which is also highly symbolic.” The backing band on the track is Duende, a Detroit-based group J has worked with extensively in the past. “Requiem for the Rose Garden” streams on Spotify, Apple Music, Tidal, Deezer and Pandora via davidjhaskins.com. ‘Postcards from the Afterlife’ due in November on 51 Recordings “Postcards from the Afterlife” is a 14-song album featuring a revolving cast of musicians and numerous autobiographical references. J sums up its themes as circling the same idea from several angles: “essentially about the poignant persistence of connection, be it in life or in death. Schisms and transitions. Love found and love lost. Requiems, reflection and revelation.” Several tracks carry string arrangements, including a finale recorded with members of the Prague Symphony and Philharmonic Orchestras. The rest of the album moves between soulful material, hazy 1960s orchestral pop, European-style chanson and the alternative rock territory J is best known for. “Postcards from the Afterlife” is released on double LP, CD and digital on 27 November. Tour dates for David J David J tours the UK through December 2026, with additional shows in Portugal, Germany and Greece around the “Postcards from the Afterlife” release. 27 November – Porto, Portugal 28 November – Lisbon, Portugal 1 December – London, UK – Moth Club 2 December – Reading, UK – Face Bar 4 December – Hebden Bridge, UK – Trades Club 5 December – Liverpool, UK – Rough Trade 8 December – Edinburgh, UK – The Voodoo Rooms 9 December – Glasgow, UK – Stereo 10 December – Newcastle, UK – The Cluny 11 December – Birmingham, UK – Hare & Hounds 13 December – Brighton, UK – Daltons 15 December – Athens, Greece – Death Disco 17 December – Berlin, Germany – Frannz Club About David J David J, born David John Haskins on 24 April 1957 in Northampton, England, co-founded Bauhaus in 1978, playing bass and co-writing songs including the group’s debut single, “Bela Lugosi’s Dead.” He sang lead vocals on “Who Killed Mr Moonlight?” Bauhaus split in 1983 and has reformed periodically since. Before Love and Rockets, J spent two years as bassist and co-producer for The Jazz Butcher, led by Pat Fish, working on the albums “A Scandal in Bohemia” (1984) and “Sex and Travel” (1985). He formed Love and Rockets in 1985 with fellow former Bauhaus members Daniel Ash and his younger brother Kevin Haskins, playing bass and sharing vocals and songwriting across seven albums released between 1985 and 1998. Both bands have reformed at intervals since their original breakups. J maintained a solo career alongside both bands. He released “Etiquette of Violence” in 1983, “Crocodile Tears and the Velvet Cosh” in 1985 and the singles compilation “On Glass” in 1986. His 1990 album “Songs from Another Season” produced the single “I’ll Be Your Chauffeur,” which reached number one on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. “Urban Urbane” followed in 1992, then “Estranged” in 2003, “Not Long for This World” in 2011 and “An Eclipse of Ships” in 2014. His memoir, “Who Killed Mister Moonlight? (Bauhaus, Black Magick and Benediction),” was published by Jawbone Press in 2014. In 2019 J released the double LP “Missive to an Angel From the Halls of Infamy and Allure.” Side-Line covered the album’s single “I Only Hear Silence Now,” featuring Emily Jane White, alongside a run of 2020 tour dates that included Bauhaus shows at Primavera Sound and Release Athens Festival. “What The Patrons Heard,” a ten-track set of originals and covers recorded over 34 years and first issued to Patreon subscribers, followed on CD and digital on 25 March 2022, with a limited numbered vinyl edition. J’s triple album of archival demos, “Tracks from the Attic,” was announced in February 2024 and released that year. He self-released the spoken-word album “The Mother Tree,” recorded with the band RAQIA, on 6 June 2025. He returned to the “Tracks from the Attic” material in March 2026 with a companion album, “Tracks From the Attic Revisited,” which Side-Line discussed with him the following month in the interview “David J Opens the Attic.” This month’s single and the album that follows continue that run of archival and new recordings.
items._cn_summary: David J（Bauhaus与Love and Rockets联合创始人）发布新单曲《Requiem for the Rose Garden》，作为专辑《Postcards from the Afterlife》的首支先行曲。该单曲由底特律乐队Duende担任伴奏，以白宫玫瑰园为象征与字面双重靶向，对特朗普政府进行抗议，创作缘起于其首个任期对花园的破坏。专辑共收录14首歌曲，主题围绕生与死中连接的恒久存续、分裂与过渡、爱与失落展开，融合自传性叙事。音乐风格跨度较大，涵盖灵魂乐素材、迷幻的1960年代管弦乐流行、欧陆香颂以及David J擅长的另类摇滚领域。部分曲目配有弦乐编配，终曲由布拉格交响乐团与爱乐乐团成员录制。整张专辑展现出对传统摇滚框架内的多风格探索，但在声音实验性或前卫性方面着墨有限，更偏向叙事驱动的歌曲创作。

items.body: Cleopatra Records will issue “Drink the New Wine”, the last studio recording by post-punk and goth rock band Bauhaus, as a 12-inch vinyl single on 30 October 2026. The pressing comes in three hand-numbered, etched color variants – white, silver and red – capped at 150 copies each, for a total of 450. Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins recorded the track separately during COVID-19 lockdown. The four traded audio files using the surrealist “exquisite corpse” method the band had used before. Bauhaus released it digitally in March 2022, its first new song since the 2008 album “Go Away White.” No Bauhaus recording has followed. Ash confirmed in April 2023 that the band’s reunion had ended, with the surviving members reforming Love and Rockets. ‘Drink the New Wine’: a lockdown recording now on hand-numbered vinyl Ash describes the track as typical of the band’s more playful side. “I always loved it when Bauhaus would go into art fart mode. Truly liberating and FUN!” he said. Cleopatra Records calls the release “a music artifact […] created for the most dedicated Bauhaus fans and collectors.” Side A of the single holds “Drink the New Wine.” Side B is etched with a reproduction of the Bauhaus logo and carries no audio. Each copy is individually hand-numbered, one color per customer, with no repressing planned once the 450 copies sell out. The single is available for pre-order through Cleopatra Records ahead of the 30 October release. About Bauhaus Small Wonder Records released Bauhaus’s debut single, “Bela Lugosi’s Dead,” in August 1979, a year after Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash, David J (David John Haskins) and his younger brother Kevin Haskins formed the band in Northampton, England. The single arrived before goth existed as a named scene. Four studio albums followed in four years on 4AD and Beggars Banquet: “In the Flat Field” (1980), “Mask” (1981), “The Sky’s Gone Out” (1982) and “Burning from the Inside” (1983). Bauhaus split on 5 July 1983, a week before “Burning from the Inside” reached shops. The pioneering band reunited for a 1998 tour and again from 2005 to 2008, a run that produced a fifth album, “Go Away White” (2008, Cooking Vinyl), released without a supporting tour. Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins had already carried their partnership into Love and Rockets, formed in 1985, and into separate solo careers. David J’s catalog includes the albums “Etiquette of Violence” and “Songs from Another Season,” plus a 2014 memoir, “Who Killed Mister Moonlight?” The four original members reunited again in 2019, announcing Peter Murphy’s first live date with Bauhaus after a heart attack ahead of shows at the Hollywood Palladium that November. A further reunion tour followed in 2022, covering Europe and the US West Coast. Months after the band released “Drink the New Wine,” Murphy’s rehab admission forced it to cancel the rest of its North American tour that August. Ash ended the reunion in April 2023, and the surviving trio returned to Love and Rockets. David J has stayed active since. He revisited his own archive on the album ‘Tracks From the Attic Revisited’ and discussed the project earlier this year in a Side-Line interview. This is the first time “Drink the New Wine” has been pressed to a physical format.
items._cn_summary: 本文为新闻报道而非乐评，介绍Bauhaus乐队最后一首录音室作品《Drink the New Wine》以限量黑胶单曲形式发行。该曲录制于新冠疫情期间，四位成员各自居家，通过超现实主义"精致尸体"创作方式交换音频文件完成合作，这也是乐队自2008年专辑《Go Away White》之后的首支新歌。限量发行共450张，分为白、银、红三色各150张手工编号版本，唱片B面无音频，仅蚀刻乐队标志。文章同时回顾了乐队自1979年发表首支单曲《Bela Lugosi's Dead》以来的历史，以及成员在Love and Rockets和个人项目中的发展轨迹。作为哥特摇滚先驱，Bauhaus与用户的暗潮/后朋克口味存在一定关联，但本文为纯新闻资讯性质，缺乏对音乐本身的深度分析，且内容偏向商业发行信息而非艺术评论。

items.body: Finnish electropunk duo I Think I Broke Something releases the single “Decadence” on 7 October 2026. The track is the third single from the duo’s upcoming EP “Another Escape,” due November 5, and the release will be marked with a show at Semifinal in Helsinki the same day. The band calls “Decadence” one of its most accessible tracks to date: “In our world, Decadence is a fairly straightforward electro-industrial punk track. You could describe it as a collision between Viagra Boys and The Prodigy, while still doing its own weird thing in its own universe. It’s probably one of the most radio-friendly tracks we’ve ever made.” Decadence by I Think I Broke Something “Decadence” follows “Illegal,” released August 6, and “Heads Up,” released September 9, as the third single from “Another Escape” ahead of the EP’s November 5 release. “Decadence” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and Spotify. About I Think I Broke Something I Think I Broke Something, also known as ITIBS, is a Helsinki-based duo made up of Jouni and Miika, active since 2014. The project debuted with the EP “Superman Sabotage Clan” and has since released three full-length albums, including “Still Not Going To,” announced for an October 26, 2022 release as the duo’s third LP, alongside numerous singles and remixes through various labels. That album cycle included the singles “Astral,” released September 2022, “Corpse,” released April 2023, and “Raw,” released July 2023. ITIBS describes its sound as a distorted electronic hybrid that draws on The Prodigy, 3TEETH and Nine Inch Nails and mixes explosive electronics with metal-heavy weight. The duo lists collaborations with The Prodigy’s Maxim, DJ Hyper and Zardonic. “Decadence,” released October 7, follows “Illegal” and “Heads Up” as the third single from the EP “Another Escape,” due November 5 alongside the band’s release show at Semifinal in Helsinki.
items._cn_summary: 芬兰双人组I Think I Broke Something发布单曲《Decadence》，这是他们即将于11月5日发行的EP《Another Escape》的第三支先行单曲。乐队自述这首歌是他们迄今最易接近的作品之一，风格被描述为电子工业朋克，融合了Viagra Boys与The Prodigy的元素。乐队2014年成立于赫尔辛基，作品以扭曲的电子混合体为核心，融合金属质感与爆发性电子节拍，此前与The Prodigy的Maxim、DJ Hyper等有过合作。本文为典型的新闻通稿式发布信息，缺少对音乐本身的实质性评论与深度分析，仅记录发行时间、曲目背景及乐队履历，信息量较为有限。

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Purwien & Kowa‘s new single “Italo-disco in San Francisco” on 9 October 2026, ahead of the German synth-pop duo’s sixth studio album, “Sechs,” due 23 October on the same label. The digital single carries four tracks: German and English versions of “Italo-disco in San Francisco,” an extended “Irgendwas ist immer (12″ Mix)” and a combined “German English Mashup 12″ mix” of the title track. Both language versions of the lyrics string together a run of 1980s references, naming figures including Lady Diana, Mikhail Gorbachev, Blondie, Phil Collins, Falco and Michael Jackson alongside songs such as “Blue Monday,” “Tainted Love,” “Like a Virgin,” “Take On Me,” “99 Luftballons,” “Forever Young” and “The Final Countdown.” “Italo-disco in San Francisco” mixes Italo disco, synthpop, New Wave and EBM, and follows the singles “Concorde” and “Hinter Glas” as the third preview of “Sechs.” Italo-disco in San Francisco by Purwien & Kowa About Purwien & Kowa Purwien & Kowa is a German synth-pop duo based in Dortmund formed by Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa. Purwien co-founded the electronic/darkwave act Second Decay in 1987, initially under the name Blue Velvet, together with Andreas Michael Sippel. Second Decay released the tape “Monochromes” in 1988 and the 12-inch “Killing Desire” in 1989, followed by “La Décadence Électronique” on CD in 1992, the “Hinter Glas” maxi-CD in 1993 and the album “Taste” in 1994. The band continued with “Der Nerv” in 1995, “Familiar” in 1997, “The Hunt” and “De Luxe” in 1998, “Hotels” in 1999 and “Kaltes, weißes Licht” in 2001, before pausing new material after the 2002 live release “Zwischenfall 1999.” Thomas Kowa, born Thomas Kowalzik in 1969 in Ludwigshafen am Rhein, joined the German synth-pop band No Comment in 1989 and has lived in Switzerland since 2007. He founded the label Nanopop in 2001, closing it in 2007 to focus on writing. Since 2012 he has published a series of crime novels and thrillers. His other current music projects include Nine Seconds and Emily Kinski’s dead. Purwien and Kowa began recording together as Purwien & Kowa, releasing the three-EP digital set “Drei” via Zwei Records in October 2018. The duo also co-hosts the Disko 80 podcast, which covers 1980s music and has featured more than 100 episodes with guests including Joachim Witt, Bernhard Lloyd of Alphaville and Marcus Meyn of Camouflage. Kowa separately co-hosts the “Krimi Schweiz” podcast on Swiss crime fiction. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Heldautomat, whose own single “Liebe ist endlich” reached Town & Towers Records on the same day as “Italo-disco in San Francisco.” The duo performed at the 18th Elektrisch Festival in 2026. Purwien & Kowa returned this year with the singles “Concorde,” “Hinter Glas” and “Italo-disco in San Francisco,” ahead of their sixth studio album, “Sechs,” produced by Olaf Wollschläger and due 23 October 2026 via Town & Towers Records.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章本质上是关于德国合成器流行双人组新单曲发行的新闻通稿，而非真正的乐评。内容主要介绍了单曲的发行信息、收录的四个版本（德语版、英语版、扩展混音和德英混合混音），以及两位成员的过往履历。歌词中串联了大量1980年代流行文化符号和经典曲目名，包括戴安娜王妃、戈尔巴乔夫、 Blondie、Phil Collins等人的名字以及《Blue Monday》《Tainted Love》《Like a Virgin》等代表作。音乐风格融合了Italo disco、合成器流行、新浪潮和EBM，延续了该组合之前单曲的路线。作为第19张专辑发行前的第三支预热单曲，此作品更偏向怀旧致敬而非艺术创新，缺乏对音乐本体深入的分析和评价。

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Heldautomat‘s new single “Liebe ist endlich” on October 9, 2026. It is the third single from the Dortmund, Germany duo’s debut album “Zwischen den Lichtern”, due October 23 on the same label. “Liebe ist endlich” (“Love is finite”) opens with a slow synthesizer introduction before settling into a synth-pop arrangement, with Christian Purwien’s vocals staying restrained throughout. The refrain states its theme directly: “Liebe ist endlich / Sie ist leider vergänglich” (“Love is finite / Unfortunately, it is transient”). Heldautomat describe the track on Bandcamp as a song with “no metaphors, no way out, no redemption. Just the quiet realisation that things come to an end.” Purwien writes the lyrics and sings. Kowa plays the synthesizers. Olaf Wollschläger produced the single. Club mix and video for ‘Liebe ist endlich’ The digital release also includes a “Videomix” of the duo’s first single, “Am ersten Tag”, and a club mix of “Liebe ist endlich” produced by Purwien & Kowa, Purwien and Kowa’s other recording project. Heldautomat also posted an official video for “Liebe ist endlich” on YouTube. “Liebe ist endlich” is open for digital pre-order on Bandcamp. Liebe ist endlich by Heldautomat About Heldautomat Heldautomat is the Dortmund, Germany duo of Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa, working with analogue synthesizers, piano and a drum machine alongside Purwien’s vocals. Purwien co-founded Second Decay in Witten in 1987 with Andreas Michael Sippel, after the pair had performed as Blue Velvet from 1985. Second Decay recorded entirely on analogue synthesizers and released albums including “Taste” (1994) and “The Hunt” (1998) before going quiet after 2002. Emmo.Biz Records has since reissued “The Hunt” on green double vinyl and “Taste” on a second double-LP edition. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Purwien & Kowa, a project with five albums behind it and a sixth, “Sechs”, in the works. The duo played the 18th Elektrisch Festival on February 27, 2026, in a set drawn 70 percent from Second Decay material. Heldautomat released its debut single, “Am ersten Tag“, on May 15, 2026. “Anders Sein” followed on August 14, reworking a song Sippel and Purwien wrote for Second Decay’s “Taste” in 1994. “Liebe ist endlich” is the third single, and precedes the October 23 album “Zwischen den Lichtern”, produced throughout by Olaf Wollschläger and including a cover of Nine Inch Nails‘ “Hurt”. A vinyl edition of the album, limited to 100 hand-signed copies, is available alongside the digital release.
items._cn_summary: Heldautomat 是来自德国多特蒙德的双人组合，使用模拟合成器、钢琴与鼓机配合人声创作。这首单曲以缓慢的合成器前奏展开，随后进入 synth-pop 编制，主唱声线全程克制内敛。歌词直白表述主题——'爱是有限的'，正如乐队在 Bandcamp 上所描述的，没有隐喻、没有出口、没有救赎，只有事物终将结束的安静认知。数字发行还包含另一首单曲的'影像混音版'以及俱乐部混音版。Purwien 同时是 Second Decay 的联合创始人，该乐队在八十年代末以纯模拟合成器录制作品并于九十年代发行过专辑。这是一篇信息性新闻稿而非深入乐评，文章内容以事实陈述为主，缺乏对音乐本身美学或创新性的分析。

items.body: This third album from the mysterious Swiss duo Blackbook was released just before the summer and brings us a total of 12 new tracks. I have always been somewhat intrigued by this act. While their music sounds superb, it is invariably driven by massive clichés and often seems almost literally ‘lifted’ from existing songs. With “Different”, they remain true to their 80s Electro-Wave/Pop influences, yet the tracks sound somewhat more personal this time around. It may be a cliché, but the way they develop their sound—consistently delivering strong choruses—is remarkable. Every single track sounds danceable and powerful, possessing the essential catchiness this genre demands. The songs also appear to have been deliberately kept short—not a single one reaches the four-minute mark. Blackbook remains a true mystery, yet one that consistently returns with great music—clichéd or not! (Rating:8½). Listen to “Nobody Loves You”: Nobody Loves You by Blackbook About Blackbook Blackbook is a Swiss duo who perform under masks and withhold their surnames, going only by their first names, Matthias and Albert. Both had previously played in other Swiss and German acts before forming Blackbook, citing 80s and 90s music as a shared influence. The duo discussed their approach and anonymity in a Side-Line interview in 2023. The project released a series of singles before compiling them into its official debut album, “Confessions Of The Innocent” (2023), followed by “Radio Strange” (2024) and, issued just before the summer of 2026, the duo’s third album “Different”, all released through darkTunes Music Group.
items._cn_summary: 这张是瑞士二人组Blackbook的第三张专辑，收录12首新歌，整体走的是80年代Electro-Wave/Pop路线。乐评指出，乐队音乐品质上乘但手法高度模式化，大量桥段和旋律走向明显借鉴既有作品。相较前作，本次的歌曲显得更加个人化，结构上保留了强劲的副歌与舞曲律动，所有曲目均控制在四分钟以内，强调了类型所需的抓耳特质。乐队成员以面具示人、仅以名相称，保持了神秘感。整体来看，这是一张在暗潮大类边缘的合成器流行专辑，舞曲属性较强，但创新性与实验性较为有限，更偏向于类型化的怀旧再现。

The Scottish post-punk and new wave band’s collection of cover versions turns 25 this year, arriving as the group’s first release after a period away from active recording. “Neon Lights” was conceived as a warm-up ahead of the following year’s “Cry” and gathers Simple Minds’ versions of songs by artists including Them, David Bowie,
items.body: Simple Minds released their twelfth studio album, “Neon Lights”, on 8 October 2001 through Eagle Records. The Scottish post-punk and new wave band’s collection of cover versions turns 25 this year, arriving as the group’s first release after a period away from active recording. “Neon Lights” was conceived as a warm-up ahead of the following year’s “Cry” and gathers Simple Minds’ versions of songs by artists including Them, David Bowie, Pete Shelley, the Patti Smith Group, Kraftwerk, the Doors, Echo and the Bunnymen, Neil Young, Roxy Music and the Velvet Underground. Frontman Jim Kerr set out the thinking behind the project at the time of release: “Neon Lights is the first time Simple Minds have put together a collection of non-original material. We thought it was appropriate at a period of looking back that we go to the very foundations of Simple Minds, which of course is the music and the bands who influenced us.” The album followed a difficult stretch for the band. Their prior record, “Our Secrets Are the Same”, had been delivered to Chrysalis but was caught up in the label’s merger with EMI, remained unreleased, and was then leaked on the internet in 2000. Discouraged by the lost momentum, band members Eddie Duffy, Mark Taylor and Mark Kerr moved on to other projects, and Jim Kerr relocated to Sicily to work part-time as a hotelier. In 2001, Kerr and guitarist Charlie Burchill began working with multi-instrumentalist Gordon “Gordy” Goudie, a former member of the Primevals, on new material intended for “Cry”. Recorded in parallel with those sessions in Glasgow, Dublin and Taormina, Sicily, “Neon Lights” was completed and released first. Simple Minds’ ‘Neon Lights’ tracklist and credits The UK edition ran ten tracks: “Gloria” (Them), “The Man Who Sold the World” (David Bowie), “Homosapien” (Pete Shelley), “Dancing Barefoot” (Patti Smith Group), “Neon Lights” (Kraftwerk), “Hello, I Love You” (the Doors), “Bring on the Dancing Horses” (Echo and the Bunnymen), “The Needle and the Damage Done” (Neil Young), “For Your Pleasure” (Roxy Music) and “All Tomorrow’s Parties” (the Velvet Underground). A US release added two further covers, “Being Boiled” (the Human League) and “Love Will Tear Us Apart” (Joy Division). The album was produced by Jim Kerr and Charlie Burchill with Gordy Goudie, except for “Gloria”, which was produced by Phunk Investigation, Daniele Tignino and Emiliano Patrik Legato; Simon Heyworth handled mastering. Two singles followed the album: the “Dancing Barefoot” EP and a series of “Homosapien” remixes. The full album is available via Spotify. About Simple Minds Simple Minds trace back to Johnny and the Self-Abusers, a Glasgow punk band formed in early 1977 by Jim Kerr, Charlie Burchill, Tony Donald and Brian McGee. That group released a single, “Saints and Sinners”, on Chiswick Records in November 1977 and split the same day. The remaining members regrouped under the name Simple Minds, drawn from a lyric in David Bowie’s “The Jean Genie”, and played their first show on 17 January 1978 in Glasgow. Duncan Barnwell joined on second guitar that January, Mick MacNeil added keyboards in March, and Derek Forbes replaced Donald on bass in April; Barnwell left by November, leaving a settled quintet of Kerr, Burchill, MacNeil, Forbes and McGee. Manager Bruce Findlay signed the band to Zoom Records, licensed to Arista, for a 1979 debut, “Life in a Day”, which reached number 30 on the UK Albums Chart. Further albums followed in quick succession: “Real to Real Cacophony” (1979), “Empires and Dance” (1980) and the double release “Sons and Fascination” / “Sister Feelings Call” (1981). Brian McGee left after those sessions and was eventually replaced by Mel Gaynor, recruited by producer Peter Walsh in 1982 and later the band’s longest-standing drummer. Released from Arista in early 1981, Simple Minds signed to Virgin Records, and “New Gold Dream” (1982) gave the band its first Billboard 200 entry and a number 3 UK placing. “Sparkle in the Rain” (1984) debuted at number 1 in the UK and was later certified Platinum, and “Once Upon a Time” (1985) reached number 1 in the UK and the Netherlands and was certified triple Platinum in Britain, driven by the US number 1 single “Don’t You (Forget About Me)” from the film “The Breakfast Club”. Bassist Derek Forbes was dismissed in the mid-1980s and replaced by John Giblin, who debuted at Live Aid in 1985. “Street Fighting Years” (1989) topped the UK chart despite Gaynor and Giblin leaving mid-session, and keyboardist Mick MacNeil quit at the close of the subsequent tour. “Real Life” (1991) and “Good News from the Next World” (1995) followed as the band’s lineup narrowed to the core of Kerr and Burchill, with Forbes and Gaynor rejoining in 1996 and 1997 respectively. “Neapolis” (1998) was the band’s only album released through Chrysalis Records. By the time of “Neon Lights” (2001), the band had regrouped around Kerr, Burchill and new recruit Gordy Goudie, who remains in the lineup today. “Cry” followed in 2002, backed by the band’s first North American tour in seven years. Simple Minds went on to release “Black & White 050505” (2005), “Graffiti Soul” (2009), which gave the band its first UK top 10 album in 14 years, “Big Music” (2014), “Acoustic” (2016), “Walk Between Worlds” (2018) and “Direction of the Heart” (2022) through BMG. The band’s catalogue has topped 60 million albums sold worldwide, and its accolades include the 2016 Ivor Novello Award for Outstanding Song Collection and the 2014 Q Inspiration Award. The current lineup pairs founders Kerr and Burchill with Goudie, Sarah Brown, Ged Grimes, Cherisse Osei and Erik Ljunggren; in September 2026 the band announced a new studio album, “Sacrosanct”, due for release on 29 January 2027. Twenty-five years after “Neon Lights”, the covers album remains the clearest record of the influences, from Kraftwerk to Joy Division, that shaped the band’s own sound.
items._cn_summary: Simple Minds 2001年发行的第十二张录音室专辑《Neon Lights》是一张翻唱专辑，收录了他们对多位影响过他们的音乐人的重新诠释，曲目涵盖Them、David Bowie、Pete Shelley、Patti Smith Group、Kraftwerk、the Doors、Echo and the Bunnymen、Neil Young、Roxy Music和Velvet Underground的作品。这张专辑诞生于乐队上一张录音室唱片因厂牌合并而未能发行的低谷期，被Jim Kerr描述为对乐队根基的回溯之作。录音在格拉斯哥、都柏林和西西里岛的陶尔米纳三地完成，与2002年专辑《Cry》的创作同步进行。文章详细列出了英国版与美版各自的曲目、附加曲目、幕后制作团队及单曲发行情况，更接近于一份专辑发行档案而非深入的评论分析。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — This one came out of the blue, thanks to the ever present and hyper-active PROG ROGUE Research and Reconnaissance Department's irascible determination to seek out new nuggets of proggy bliss. The Freiburg based band has some seasoned musicians who have a communicative style, maximizing on emotional delivery and instrumental dexterity. The tracks are exceedingly melodic, quintessentially adventurous in that they combine ornate passion with gritty exaltation and raised my tired eyebrows more than once, and on each track! I went through this once while driving for work and I caught myself stopping a few times to marvel at my good fortune.The opener "Way to Cydonia" initially does open on a martial pulse, serving to assert the musical qualities of the players, what with the crunchy guitars and riffling keys but the mood immediately changes when the perfidious bass and smacking drums set the stage for the convincing vocal line, piano in tow as the arrangement expands in scope and sinks deep into the mind. The soft middle section is achingly beautiful , the piano and voice (lead and harmony) elevating to the choral melee with the tortuous lead guitar carving menacingly , as the rhythmic fury reaches a paroxysm. 'Sturm und Drang'!Now, here was the clincher! The next piece "Where is the Silence" was where I halted the first time on the autobahn, a delightfully melancholic, crushingly poignant tune that coalesces that stunning piano and elegant voice into an aural embrace verging on restrained perfection. A hymn for our times and a panacea for the soul. 'Ausgezeichnet'!The epic "Union of Souls" clocks in at 14 minutes + and falls into that classic progressive mold that elects to take its time in developing structure whilst telling an adventure. The initial section is measured in mellow despondence , until that moment where the atmosphere moves to a higher instrumental plain with a plaintive acoustic guitar phrasing at first, then a slowly expanding bass line, distant keyboard panting, marshaling drum beat and echoing pools of keys. When the volatile fury arrives, its purely orgasmic, a sizzling guitar streaks the sky, with mellotrons in tow. When singer Michael Bernauer clutches the microphone, his elegiac delivery veers from sullen to accepting. Majestic, powerful, lush and utterly moving. 'Wunderbar'!As proof of their professionalism, the band opts for two live tracks, which can be a risky move in some instances, but not here. On the contrary, the public display stamped this immediately with all the credentials need for a pentagon award. "Caravan of Slaves" begins with applause and military snare with thunderous percussives, as the caravan wanders into the sandstorm. Twirling synths and snake guitar lines serve up the Middle eastern theme perfectly, switching into a sweltering mini-jam session where each member is introduced on its instrument, the rotund bass guitar killing it as it rumbles over the dunes, aided by oasis guitars, palm tree keyboards and dromedary thumping drums. When they all coalesce into one musical pyramid, it's a pure joy to behold. I stopped again on the motorway as the word fun came to mind, or in German: 'Viel Spass'!The second live track "Already There" has a ghostly Floydian feel, with effect-laden voice in the hazy spotlight, a desperate whisper along with a doleful plea within a whopping melody and chorus that welds deep into the mind. Clanging guitar and Masonian beat keeps the mood reflective, spooky Wright keys and a fine electric guitar foray, right out of the Gilmourian manual. The harrowing vocal finale is simply devastating! 'Schon da'!I enjoyed this from the very first audition and subsequent revisits have only served to solidify my impressions! After all, both the Rogue and the Laz cannot be wrong at the same, that would be 'unm�glich' (Impossible). More, bitte!4.5 Martian Craters

items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — Crime of the Century is an album that manages to balance the accessibility of pop rock with elements of greater musical complexity. Although it is often associated with Progressive Rock, I see it more as a progressive pop rock album, using progressive elements without fully committing to the more complex characteristics of the genre. This is especially evident in tracks such as "School" and "Rudy", which feature more elaborate structures and development.One of the album's greatest strengths is precisely this balance between melody and sophistication. The songs are quite accessible, but they never feel simplistic. There is clearly a lot of attention to arrangements, dynamics and development, allowing the album to work both as a collection of great melodies and as a record with plenty of interesting musical details.Among the tracks, "School" is one of the major highlights, with an excellent combination of atmosphere, instrumentation and development. "Hide in Your Shell" is also one of my favorites and, in particular, one of the tracks that best represents what I find special about this album. "Bloody Well Right" and "Asylum" are also excellent, while "Dreamer", despite being a very good song, takes a more direct and accessible approach.The instrumentation is another strong point. The saxophone is particularly distinctive and contributes greatly to the album's identity. The keyboards also play an important role, although I find the saxophone more impressive overall. The drums are very well played, while the guitar and bass are effective without necessarily being the instruments that stand out the most.But the biggest vocal highlight is undoubtedly Roger Hodgson. His voice has a very distinctive character and is immediately recognizable. His high register and particular way of delivering melodies give Supertramp an identity that I find difficult to compare with other bands. The vocal melodies are excellent and are probably among the strongest aspects of the entire album. Rick Davies also delivers very good vocals, but Hodgson's voice is more memorable to me.The production has aged extremely well. The mixing is excellent, and the instruments are very clearly defined, allowing each element to be heard without difficulty. The album has a very balanced sound and still works remarkably well decades after its release. A particularly interesting production moment is the final section of "Asylum", which creates a very engaging atmosphere.I also consider the themes of the album to be important. There is a predominantly melancholic atmosphere connected to the human and social issues addressed throughout the songs. Subjects such as education, isolation and other recurring social problems appear in different forms. The title Crime of the Century itself can be interpreted as a criticism of the problems created by society and the kind of prison that society can impose on individuals.The cover reinforces this idea very effectively. The image of what appears to be a prison fits the atmosphere of the album and can be interpreted as a symbolic representation of society and the limitations it imposes. It is a cover that I consider extremely appropriate for the album's content.Despite its qualities, I do not consider Crime of the Century one of the greatest examples of Progressive Rock in the strictest sense of the genre. Its historical importance is significant, but I believe there are many albums that are much more progressive and representative of the genre. For this reason, I would not necessarily recommend it as an introduction to Progressive Rock. It can work very well as a bridge between rock/pop and progressive music, but there are bands with much more complex approaches and much stronger connections to the genre.I also do not consider the album particularly innovative in terms of progressive music, although it contains some interesting ideas and has a very strong individual identity. In fact, one of the most difficult things about it is finding other bands to compare it with, since Supertramp has a very distinctive sound of its own.Among its strongest points are the very well-defined instrumentation, especially the saxophone and keyboards, Roger Hodgson's vocals, and the themes behind the songs. I do not see many significant weaknesses in the album. My main reservation concerns the final tracks: although they are good, I find the first part of the album stronger and more memorable. "Crime of the Century", the title track, is the song that impresses me the least, although I still consider it a good composition.Overall, I consider Crime of the Century a very good album, with an excellent balance between accessibility, strong melodies, sophisticated instrumentation, distinctive vocals and social themes. The opening tracks, especially "School" and "Hide in Your Shell", are among its greatest highlights, and the production remains impressive.It is not, for me, an essential Progressive Rock album in the strictest sense of the genre, but it is a high-quality record with a very strong identity. Its ability to naturally combine pop rock with progressive elements is precisely what makes it special.
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年专辑在流行摇滚的可听性与渐进摇滚的复杂度之间寻求平衡，旋律突出但不过度简化，编曲与动态发展颇具匠心。萨克斯是专辑最具辨识度的乐器，与键盘共同塑造了独特的声场，鼓点扎实，Roger Hodgson的高音域嗓音赋予乐队难以模仿的标志性音色。主题围绕教育、孤独与社会批判展开，封面设计强化了关于社会囚禁的隐喻。整体制作精良，经得起时间考验。然而，作为带有渐进元素的流行摇滚，其音乐语汇偏向主流，缺乏实验性突破和跨领域融合，与前卫、实验、爵士或电子等口味的距离较远。

items.body: New England goth and post-punk band Ghost Painted Sky released the maxi-single “Kissing Lions” on October 6, 2026. The release previews the band’s upcoming second full-length album, “Failure Blooms.” The maxi-single carries three tracks: the title song, a “Kissing Lions (Effervescent Remix),” and “My Words Are Not My Own,” a new track that leans toward the band’s synthpop influences. Lisa Wood wrote the lyrics and sings. David Strong plays guitar, bass, ebow, drums and programming, and synths, and co-wrote the lyrics. Michael Boudreau contributes additional guitar and Aurora Grabill plays violin on both versions of “Kissing Lions.” William Faith of Faith and the Muse mixed and mastered the title track at his own 13 Studio. The remix and “My Words Are Not My Own” were mixed by Strong and mastered by Faith at the same studio. Strong also made the cover art, a stylized still from the “Kissing Lions” video. Kissing Lions by Ghost Painted Sky Ghost Painted Sky described “Kissing Lions” in the release’s Bandcamp notes: “those mostly vain attempts to seize on anything that creates a fleeting feeling of being alive for a moment amid relentless waves of the humdrum, doldrums, and failure […] bad decisions that bite back and create further downward spirals.” Ghost Painted Sky also put out an official video for “Kissing Lions.” “Kissing Lions” is available now as a digital download and via streaming on Bandcamp. About Ghost Painted Sky Ghost Painted Sky began in 2014 as the solo studio project of David Strong, who released a self-titled debut EP that year. A second short EP, “The Shadows Breath,” followed in 2015, alongside the band’s first live shows. Lisa Wood joined on vocals in 2018, starting with the “Scars” EP and continuing on the group’s debut full-length album, “Flightless”. Wood has since become the band’s primary vocalist. The band appeared on several compilations through the early 2020s, including “The Unquiet Grave 2020” (Cleopatra Records, 2020), “33 Gothic Bands You Should Know, Volume 8” (Post-Gothic, 2021), “You Are Still Not Alone” (Darkness Calling, 2021) and “Goths For Sanctuaries – The Album!!!” (2023). It released the “Ephemeral Wake” EP in 2021, followed by the singles “Corridors” in 2022 and “Insomnia” in 2024. Ghost Painted Sky is now finishing its second full-length album, “Failure Blooms,” with new studio contributions from guitarist Michael Boudreau and longtime live keyboardist and violinist Aurora Grabill. “Sound and Fury,” the album’s first single, came out in late March 2026, also mixed and mastered by Faith at 13 Studio. “Kissing Lions” is the second single, with “Failure Blooms” expected later in 2026.
items._cn_summary: Ghost Painted Sky这支来自新英格兰的哥特与后朋克乐队发布了单曲集《Kissing Lions》，收录三首作品，包括标题曲、Effervescent混音版以及偏向合成器流行方向的新曲《My Words Are Not My Own》。歌词与演唱由Lisa Wood担纲，David Strong负责吉他、贝斯、鼓、合成器及大部分编曲，另邀小提琴与吉他客座乐手参与。由Faith and the Muse的William Faith在13 Studio完成混音。乐队描述作品主题为对琐碎生活中短暂鲜活感的徒劳追逐以及错误决策引发的下行漩涡。文章以新闻稿格式罗列专辑人员、制作背景与乐队履历，未对音乐本体进行实质性的乐评分析。

items.body: Review by Matti — The focus wasn't very sharp yet, when the newly formed Amsterdam-based quartet went to London to record their debut album in January 1970. At the time they had secured a five-month slot at the Amsterdam cast of the hippie musical Hair. Of course the musicians, namely guitarist Jan Akkerman and Thijs van Leer (organ, piano, vocals), with a rhythm section that was to be replaced for the next album, already had several years' experience in rock music, separately. If this album (and the band) was a one-off case instead of being a prelude to the all-time greatest chapter of Dutch prog, undoubtedly it would be at least a "hidden prog gem" or maybe even an established early classic. But Focus was to reach so much higher levels that if the already charmed listener at some point enters their debut, it won't be an ubforgettable affair. Three stars is the best I can give.Focus at their prime (and ever since) were very much an instrumental act, so the large amount of vocal pieces is the most interesting feature here. The nearly 10-minute opener 'Focus' is, however, an instrumental and surely shows the way the band was heading at, but I can't help feeling it simply loses its focus and feels over-extended,despite containing beautiful melodies. Akkerman's electric guitar solo lacks elegance and goes on too long. 'Why Dream' is a 4-minute ballad-ish song sung by Thijs with bassist Martijn Dresden's backing vocals. Slightly reminiscent of the obscure, late 60's Pink Floyd songs sung by Rick Wright, except that the electric guitar dominates the latter half.The drug dealing lyrics for 'Happy Nightmare (Mescaline)' were written by Mike Hayes for Dresden particularily. This rather peaceful song has a nice jazzy flair, and the guitar solo, unlike on the previous track, is thankfully followed by a brief return to the song substance. The dynamic 7-minute instrumental 'Anonymus' suffers from the similar blurred focus and the taste of unnecessary extension as 'Focus'. The Focus trademarks, even a hint of Old Music, are there, but in a jam-like form to show off the group's technical competence, especially speaking of their most recent member Akkerman whose classically influenced composing skills are only carefully starting to bloom on this album.'Black Beauty' is an OK melodic song that - without the irritatingly sharp-sounding guitar - would pass as a mediocre Moody Blues song c. 1968. 'Sugar Island' is a merry song about Cuba with silly lyrics. No wonder it was omitted from the album's US edition. The serene closing piece 'Focus (Vocal)' is a little revisitation to a theme heard on the opener, featuring calm and terribly brief vocals, but somehow even it, in less than 3 minutes, loses the focus and just continues the simple musical phrase. Pretty but boring.The lively, Jethro Tull reminding flute-heavy instrumental 'House of King' was wisely added to the album's later editions. It has the sharp rhythm a bit too much on the surface, but otherwise it's charming in its simplicity. All in all, this debut has no ghost of a chance competing with the real Focus classics.
items._cn_summary: 这是荷兰四人乐队Focus的1970年首张专辑，吉他手Jan Akkerman与键盘手/主唱Thijs van Leer为核心。彼时乐队成员尚未完全成型，录制时刚从阿姆斯特丹音乐剧《Hair》的驻场演出中抽出。与乐队后来成熟期以器乐曲为主不同，这张专辑包含相当比例的人声曲目。开篇器乐曲《Focus》近十分钟，旋律优美但结构松散延伸过度；抒情曲《Why Dream》人声风格类似晚期Pink Floyd的Rick Wright。《Happy Nightmare (Mescaline)》歌词涉及毒品题材，吉他独奏处理更为节制。器乐曲《Anonymus》同样存在冗长问题，展示成员的技术能力却缺少凝聚力。《Black Beauty》旋律尚可但吉他音色刺耳，《Sugar Island》歌词戏谑因而被美版删除。后期版本收录的《House of King》flute元素令人联想到Jethro Tull，但节奏过于表面化。整张专辑虽已显露乐队潜力雏形，但相比后期作品显得粗糙、缺乏焦点，最终被乐评给予三颗星评价。

items.body: English musician Bruce Gilbert, a founding member of Wire, plays a solo live set at Café OTO in London on Friday 9 October 2026. The night is billed as “The Hotel presents…” and also features Rocheman and performance artist Finn Kennedy. Doors are at 7:30pm, with tickets priced from £13 for Café OTO members up to £20 on the door, available through the venue. The show is The Hotel’s third evening at Café OTO in 2026. Gilbert’s set previews a new album due from The Hotel later this year. Test pressings of the as-yet-unannounced record will be sold at the merch table. Finn Kennedy premieres a newly commissioned piece titled “Streams.” Rocheman closes the night with a full band set, performing as a quartet with Fred Lomas on lead guitar, Tom Powell on drums and Tom Wright on keyboards. Rocheman’s second album, “Basin,” was released on vinyl by The Hotel earlier in 2026, following the EPs “Angel Storm” and “Virtua Saint” on Mindseyerecords.xyz. The self-directed feature film “Taurus,” due in 2027, is among the artist’s forthcoming work. Tickets for The Hotel at Café OTO Tickets cost £13 for Café OTO members, £17 in advance and £20 on the door, available through the venue’s event page. About Bruce Gilbert Bruce Gilbert, born Bruce Clifford Gilbert on 18 May 1946 in Watford, England, co-founded Wire in London in 1976 alongside Colin Newman, Graham Lewis and Robert Gotobed, playing guitar in the band until he left in 2004, following the release of the album “Send.” After Wire’s first breakup in 1980, Gilbert formed a series of projects with bassist Graham Lewis, including Cupol, Dome, P’o and Duet Emmo. Side-Line covered the 2022 remastered reissue of Duet Emmo’s sole album, “Or So It Seems,” Gilbert’s trio recording with Lewis and Daniel Miller. Gilbert also worked with A.C. Marias, producing the single “Drop/So” in 1980 for the group’s Dome label and co-producing the 1989 album “One of Our Girls (Has Gone Missing),” sharing songwriting credit with Angela Conway. Gilbert’s solo albums include “This Way” (1984), “The Shivering Man” (1987) and “Ab Ovo” (1996), all released on Mute, followed by “Ordier” (2004), “Oblivio Agitatum” (2009, Editions Mego) and “Diluvial” (2013, Touch), a collaboration with BAW. He also performs as a DJ under the name DJ Beekeeper. Wire continued without Gilbert after his departure, releasing the mini-album “Nocturnal Koreans” in 2016. Gilbert now appears at Café OTO as part of The Hotel’s third London show of 2026, ahead of a new album the label is set to release later this year.

items.body: Marilyn Manson’s second studio album, “Antichrist Superstar,” turns 30 this year. The band released the record on 8 October 1996 through Nothing and Interscope Records. A rock opera and concept album, it followed 1994’s “Portrait of an American Family” and the 1995 EP “Smells Like Children,” and was recorded over roughly eight months at Nothing Studios in New Orleans. The album was produced by Marilyn Manson together with Trent Reznor, Dave Ogilvie and Sean Beavan, with Ogilvie departing partway through the sessions and Beavan brought in to finish the record with the band. Guitarist Daisy Berkowitz left the group during recording and was replaced by Zim Zum shortly after the album’s completion, with bassist Twiggy Ramirez performing the majority of the guitar parts. The 16-track CD, split into three sections titled “The Heirophant,” “Inauguration of the Worm” and “Disintegrator Rising,” runs “Irresponsible Hate Anthem,” “The Beautiful People,” “Dried Up, Tied and Dead to the World,” “Tourniquet,” “Little Horn,” “Cryptorchid,” “Deformography,” “Wormboy,” “Mister Superstar,” “Angel with the Scabbed Wings,” “Kinderfeld,” “Antichrist Superstar,” “1996,” “Minute of Decay,” “The Reflecting God” and “Man That You Fear,” followed by a hidden track, “Empty Sounds of Hate.” Album artwork was designed by P. R. Brown using photography by Dean Karr. “Antichrist Superstar” debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 and has sold close to two million copies in the United States. Lead single “The Beautiful People” preceded the album on 22 September 1996 and reached number 26 on Billboard’s Modern Rock Tracks chart and the top 20 of the UK Singles Chart, followed by second single “Tourniquet” on 8 September 1997, which peaked at number 28 in the UK. The album is the first installment of a trilogy the band completed with “Mechanical Animals” (1998) and “Holy Wood (In the Shadow of the Valley of Death)” (2000), and was supported by the year-long Dead to the World Tour. About Marilyn Manson Marilyn Manson formed in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, in 1989, when singer Brian Warner – who took the stage name Marilyn Manson – paired with guitarist Scott Putesky, known as Daisy Berkowitz. Performing initially as Marilyn Manson & the Spooky Kids, the group built a South Florida following through theatrical live shows, with a lineup that came to include bassist Brad Stewart (Gidget Gein), keyboardist Stephen Bier (Madonna Wayne Gacy) and drummer Fred Streithorst (Sara Lee Lucas). In 1993, Nine Inch Nails founder Trent Reznor signed the band as the first act on his Nothing Records label and produced their debut album, “Portrait of an American Family,” released on 19 July 1994. The “Smells Like Children” EP followed in 1995, featuring a cover of the Eurythmics’ “Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)”; Jeordie White, performing as Twiggy Ramirez, had by then replaced Gein on bass. “Antichrist Superstar” followed on 8 October 1996, co-produced by Reznor, Marilyn Manson, Dave Ogilvie and Sean Beavan, and debuted at number three on the Billboard 200 behind lead single “The Beautiful People.” The album’s success coincided with the departure of founding guitarist Daisy Berkowitz and the arrival of Zim Zum, and the band supported the record with the Dead to the World Tour. The group’s next album, “Mechanical Animals,” arrived on 15 September 1998, followed by “Holy Wood (In the Shadow of the Valley of Death)” in 2000, closing out the self-described triptych that “Antichrist Superstar” opened. Thirty years after its release, the album remains the first chapter of that trilogy.

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The beginning of a new era: the Steve Hogarth era. (Thank you, Darryl Way!)1. "The King of Sunset Town" (8:02) how anyone elevates this band's compositional, instrumental, and sound production skill at the level or even above that of contemporaries IQ, Pendragon, or even Pallas is beyond me! This is so much less! So much prog lite. Steve Hogarth is just one of the rabble when he tries to belt it out like his contemporaries but when he slows it down and expresses from the depths of his delicate soul he is a force to be reckoned with. (13/15)2. "Easter" (5:57) okay music, okay sound production, okay vocal and lyric, corny, simplistic keyboard work; nice drumming, bass, and lead guitar work. (8.75/10)3. "The Uninvited Guest" (3:52) anyone for some BON JOVI? or BRYAN ADAMS? How 'bout some RICHARD MARX? or even Foreigner and latter-day REO Speedwagon or Def Leppard? Here you have it! (8.75/10)4. "Seasons End" (8:07) nice vocal performance by Steve over some weak and saccharine keyboard and guitar arpeggios. The synth washes and piano chords and Pete Trewavas' bass work make it more tolerable. I wish Steve's voice had been mixed more forward/loudly in the final soundscape. In the third minute the sound levels ramp up while Steve H. rests and Steve R. takes over. Nice passage despite the bombastic snare-and-tom rims hits. The sixth minute yields to a whole new motif: one that is founded in glockenspiel pixie dust and other keyboard MIDI sounds meant to emulate dream world scenarios. Another lesson that instructs us as to how one can make much out of very little. (13.5/15)5. "Holloway Girl" (4:27) rotating four-chord keyboard progressions set the stage for this unorthodox Duke "Behind the Lines"-like ballad. (8.75/10)6. "Berlin" (7:43) finally a song construct that is a little more adventurous, a little more nuanced. While there is an undeniable ALAN PARSONS PROJECT sound and feel to this, it has the subtle sophistication of something more poignant, more poetic. I never thought I'd ever be extolling the presence of a saxophone as an enhancing effect but Phil Todd's play here does, in fact, elevate the music to another level. Nice atmospheric passage in the fourth minute to bridge into the song's climactic second half. I do not like Steve R's bottle neck guitar sound but I love Pete Trewavas' bass blasts--and then full-power palette of the sixth minute with Steve H's great list recitation and Steve R.'s excellent rhythm guitar pickings. Very cool! Easily the best two minutes on the album. (13.75/15)7. "After Me" (3:19) � picked 12-string acoustic guitar chords sound a bit like ELP's "Lucky Man" but the chords are different and Steve H's vocal melody lines are quite different--more akin to something from BON JOVI or JOHN COUGAR MELLENCAMP. Mark's MIDIed keyboard arpeggi in the second half of the second minute seem to relieve Steve R from his 12-string duties so he can pick up his electric axe. From here the song becomes just another from the day. Too bad. (8.75/10)8. "Hooks in You" (2:54) an opening that was lifted by Poland's COLLAGE for the fifth song of their 1991 album, Moonshine, "The Blues." It's too bad that I can't stop hearing that iconic song while listening to this one. Otherwise, it's a pretty good RICHARD MARX song. (8.75/10)9. "The Space..." (6:14) bouncy two-chord MIDI-ed synth strings keyboard chords slowly rise to the surface as the rest of the band and the two Steves join in, At 1:50 there is a switch into some heavier power chord to back Steve H during the chorus, but then we're back into the main motif of the verse for a bit before Steve H's rhythm guitar chord play leads the band into some more contemplative/reflective music and then, in the fifth minute, into a brief instrumental solo section. But then everything cuts out save for Mark's synth string washes and Steve H's 'distant' "everybody in the whole of the world" strainings. Cool section--cool vocal work (and music to support). And then it's done! (9/10)Total Time 50:35Hogarth trying to sound like Genesis, Paul Carrack (Ace, Mike + The Mechanics), or Paul Menel (IQ) doesn't work: he just becomes one of the many, but when Hogarth slows it down and brings in his sensitive approach he becomes something else: his own man, his own force, his own unique artist. � not included on vinyl LP releases (on CD only)B-/four stars; a solid NeoProg album that does beg for a little more sophistication and a little more maturity in the compositional department.

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — The third album of my beloved Procol Harum, "A salty dog". The last one with Dave Knights on bass guitar and the last one as well with Matthew Fisher on keys, who he also did the production on this one. Now, "A salty dog", is a much more laid-back record than the two previous of the band, yet is so so beautiful. Mostly blues-based with a progressive direction, and always having the distinctive Procol Harum sound, meaning piano and voice driven. When Gary Brooker first performed the piece "A salty dog" on piano, the room was filled with sunlight shining through the windows. The drummer, B.J. Wilson, with a sunbeam on his face, told Brooker he thought it was the most beautiful song he had ever heard. Gary Brooker delivers some vein-cutting vocals throughout the album. Matthew Fisher did the lead vocals on three tracks on this one, "Boredom", "Wreck of the Hesperus" and "Pilgrim's progress". The track "Crucifiction" is a lament with ripping lead vocals provided by Robin Trower. A really beautiful album, closing a chapter for Procol Harum.
items._genre: crossover prog / blues rock / classic rock
items._cn_summary: 《A Salty Dog》是Procol Harum的第三张专辑，标志着乐队一个阶段的结束——这是Dave Knights和Matthew Fisher最后参与的唱片。整体氛围较前两张更为内敛放松，以蓝调为底色融入渐进摇滚的方向，钢琴与人声主导的乐队特色贯穿始终。Gary Brooker的演唱充满情感张力，Matthew Fisher在三首曲目中担任主唱，Robin Trower则在《Crucifiction》中贡献了撕裂感十足的演唱。专辑融合了诗歌化的歌词叙事与英伦摇滚的优雅气质，在编曲上注重器乐层次的铺陈。该作被视作乐队成熟期的代表作之一，为后续风格转变划下了句点。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Released in 2007 through the bands official fan club, 'Images and Words 15th Anniversary Performance' is literally what it says it is; Dream Theater playing the entire album that forever set the standard for all progressive metal bands to follow. Of course, it has its pros and cons. There's some interesting embellishments dotted around, which could keep us prog nerds at least somewhat invested for a little while, and it's cool to hear Jordan Rudess interpret some of Kevin Moore's keyboard parts. Then of course, there's vocalist James LaBrie. Sure, he struggles with some of it due to age and a well-documented vocal injury, but I guess at least he's trying. The band would go on to release a 25th anniversary performance of this album through their 'Lost Not Forgotten' series many years later, so, you know, it's probably slightly better than that one, again, due to LaBrie being another ten years older by then and struggling even more. Bless him. I don't think I'd ever choose to actually listen to this over the original 1992 studio album, which, for the record, is my favourite album of all time. But the name of this release describes exactly what you're getting here, so there's absolutely no point in taking it too seriously. It's a cool addition to the collection, and if you're a die-hard Dream Theater fan like I am, then you'll enjoy owning it. Simple as that.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dream Theater 2007年通过官方粉丝俱乐部发行的现场录音，内容为完整重演其1992年经典专辑《Images and Words》。评论指出，现场版本加入了一些编曲装饰和键盘即兴处理，鲁德斯的键盘部分与原版摩尔诠释有所不同。主唱拉布里因年龄增长和声带伤病的困扰，演绎原版高难度旋律时显得力不从心。评论将其与2020年发行的25周年版本进行比较，认为本版本因主唱状态稍好而略胜，但仍无法超越原始录音室版本。这张专辑本质上是收藏品，适合铁杆粉丝，整体忠实复刻原作但缺乏新的艺术突破，属于典型的乐队纪念性现场发行作品。

items.excerpt: 2026.10.07 ベルリン在住約30年の音楽評論家・ジャーナリスト、城所孝吉が語る 世界最高峰のオーケストラとして知られるベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団。その魅力は、いったいどこにあるのでしょうか。1994年からベルリンを拠点に活動し、2012年から10年間、ベルリン・フィルのメディア部門で日本向けマーケティングや事業開発にも携わった音楽ジャーナリスト、城所孝吉さんに、演奏の特徴や歴代指揮者との関係、音楽家たちの姿勢について聞きました。 ※本記事はポッドキャスト番組『ONTOMO Radio』で語られた内容を再構成しています。 ONTOMO編集部 東京・神楽坂にある音楽之友社を拠点に、Webマガジン「ONTOMO」の企画・取材・編集をしています。「音楽っていいなぁ、を毎日に。」を掲げ、やさしく・ふかく・おもしろ... 詳しく見る 世界のオーケストラが意識するベルリン・フィル ——ベルリン・フィルと他の一流オーケストラには、どのような違いがあるのでしょうか？ 城所 他のオーケストラと比べると、彼らの置かれている状況が違うと思います。以前、ドイツで別のいくつかのオーケストラの広報活
items.body: 2026.10.07 ベルリン在住約30年の音楽評論家・ジャーナリスト、城所孝吉が語る 世界最高峰のオーケストラとして知られるベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団。その魅力は、いったいどこにあるのでしょうか。1994年からベルリンを拠点に活動し、2012年から10年間、ベルリン・フィルのメディア部門で日本向けマーケティングや事業開発にも携わった音楽ジャーナリスト、城所孝吉さんに、演奏の特徴や歴代指揮者との関係、音楽家たちの姿勢について聞きました。 ※本記事はポッドキャスト番組『ONTOMO Radio』で語られた内容を再構成しています。 ONTOMO編集部 東京・神楽坂にある音楽之友社を拠点に、Webマガジン「ONTOMO」の企画・取材・編集をしています。「音楽っていいなぁ、を毎日に。」を掲げ、やさしく・ふかく・おもしろ... 詳しく見る 世界のオーケストラが意識するベルリン・フィル ——ベルリン・フィルと他の一流オーケストラには、どのような違いがあるのでしょうか？ 城所 他のオーケストラと比べると、彼らの置かれている状況が違うと思います。以前、ドイツで別のいくつかのオーケストラの広報活動も担当していたのですが、私がベルリン・フィルでも仕事をしていると聞くと、どこへ行っても「うちだってあれくらい弾ける」と言われるんです。他のオーケストラも一流ですし、実際に演奏も素晴らしい。なのに、ベルリン・フィルを引き合いに出して話すんです。 城所孝吉（きどころ・たかよし） 1970年生まれ。ドイツ・ベルリン在住。早稲田大学第一文学部ドイツ文学専修を卒業後、ベルリン自由大学、工科大学に留学。在学中より音楽評論家、ジャーナリストとして活動し、朝日新聞、毎日新聞、読売新聞等の日刊紙、『レコード芸術ONLINE』『音楽の友』『ぶらあぼ』『モーストリークラシック』等の専門誌に寄稿する。2003年からは音楽ビジネスに関わり、TDKヨーロッパで音楽DVDを制作。欧州の著名オーケストラのパブリシストを務めたあと、2012年以降は、10年間にわたりベルリン・フィルのメディア部門「ベルリン・フィル・メディア」で、配信サービス「デジタル・コンサートホール」の日本向けマーケティング、事業開発に従事した。2022年に、ドイツ・グラモフォンに移籍。2026年まで、アジア市場における事業開発、録音制作(A&R)に携わった。 ——それだけ、ベルリン・フィルが比較の対象になっているということですね。 城所 そうです。他のオーケストラから常に見られている、ある意味で監視されているような状況にあるわけです。ウィーン・フィルはまた別で、ウィーンという土地に根ざした独自のブランドや音楽性があります。誰かがまねをしようとしても、簡単にはできないものですよね。一方、ベルリン・フィルは、他のオーケストラが「自分たちだってできる」と言いたくなる存在なんです。 ベルリンでは、外から来るオーケストラも、フィルハーモニーという同じ舞台で演奏します。ウィーン・フィルやロンドン交響楽団など、世界の一流オーケストラが訪れると、それぞれが最高の演奏をしようとする。ベルリン・フィルは、そうした演奏を聴く人々の視線も意識せざるを得ない。世界のトップにいることを守るために、常に実力を出し切る必要があるのだと思います。 ベルリン・フィルハーモニー大ホールの内観 カラヤンからアバドへ、変化した音楽家の関係 ——長年ベルリン・フィルを見てきて、オーケストラの変化をどのように感じていますか？ 城所 大きな転換点の一つは、カラヤンからアバドへの交代です。カラヤンの時代は、いわば巨匠がオーケストラを支配するスタイルでした。団員による室内楽活動もありましたが、演奏会ではカラヤンが主導していた。 それに対してアバドは、団員と一緒に音楽をつくろうとしたんです。アバドは、自分のことを「クラウディオ」と呼んでほしいと言っていたことでも知られています。団員一人ひとりが責任を持ち、自分の考えを出し合い、互いに目を合わせ、呼吸をしながら、室内楽のように一つの音楽をつくっていく。そういう民主的なオーケストラへと変えていったのだと思います。 ——その変化は、のちの指揮者にも影響したのでしょうか？ 城所 アバドの時代に団員の自主性が高まっていった。その後を引き継いだラトルは、そうして変化したベルリン・フィルと16年間、格闘したというのが私の印象です。成功することもあれば、そうでないこともあった。ラトルとオーケストラの関係は、決して一筋縄ではいかなかったと思います。 カラヤン指揮／ベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団『ベートーヴェン：交響曲第5番、第6番』 アバド指揮／ベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団『ベートーヴェン：交響曲第5番、第6番』 ラトル最後の演奏会に見た16年間の関係 ——ラトルの最後の演奏会では、マーラーの交響曲第6番が演奏されました。 城所 私はその演奏会に行って、本当に感動しました。それまでベルリン・フィルとラトルは、いろいろとやり合ってきたという印象があったんです。でも最後の演奏会では、団員たちが彼のために涙をこらえるように、顔を真っ赤にして演奏していました。それを見て、これは本物の、特別な関係だったんだと、ようやく納得できたんです。 マーラーの第6番には、最後に勝ったのか負けたのかわからないまま終わる、という解釈があります。ラトルは、ベルリン・フィルとの関係も、どちらが勝ったのかわからないまま終わるという意味を込めて、この曲を選んだのではないか。私はそう考えました。イギリス人らしい辛口のユーモア、ブラックユーモアなのかもしれないと思っていたのですが、実際の演奏会はそうした想像とは違っていました。団員たちの演奏から、ラトルとの関係が伝わってきたんです。 サイモン・ラトル指揮／ベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団『マーラー：交響曲第６番』 ペトレンコが築くこれからのベルリン・フィル ——現在の首席指揮者、ペトレンコについてはどのように見ていますか？ 城所 ペトレンコが選ばれたとき、私はこの人でよかったと思いました。作品を深く読み込む力があり、自分の解釈を深めていける指揮者だと思うからです。楽譜を徹底的に読み、完璧を目指すところもあります。一方で、今は少し考えすぎているように感じることもあります。 例えば、縦の線を非常に精密に合わせることへのこだわりがあります。ベルリン・フィルには、音楽の流れのなかで生まれる揺れや、感情的なフレージングがあります。そこに精密さが加わることで、非常に緊張感の高い演奏になる一方、少し窮屈に感じられる場合もある。今は、そのぎりぎりのところにいるように思います。 ただ、作品の深部を読み込む力がある指揮者は、これからも成長していくと思います。ペトレンコはまだこれから変わっていくでしょうし、もっと自由になっていくのではないかと期待しています。 キリル・ペトレンコ指揮によるベルリン・フィルとの初録音『チャイコフスキー：交響曲第６番』 ——そんなベルリンの音楽現場を長年見てきた城所さんの新刊が、『ベルリンから見た不思議おもしろ音楽事情 気分はカプリッチョ』です。ベルリン・フィルだけでなく、ヨーロッパの音楽や文化、音楽ビジネスなど、幅広いテーマを扱っています。 城所 この本は、ベルリンに軸足を置いて、さまざまなことを観察し、考察したものです。日本とヨーロッパではものの見方が違うことがありますよね。その違いを取り上げて、「なぜ違うのか」を考えると、読者にも「なるほど」と楽しんでもらえると思いました。 ——ベルリンの街で往年の名歌手に遭遇した話から、コロナや政治、音楽をめぐる問題まで、軽い話題も考えさせられるテーマも織り交ぜられていますね。 城所 音楽の話って、難しくしようと思えばいくらでも難しくできる。でも、難しいことをわかってもらうためには、面白く話をすればいいと思うんです。 書籍情報『ベルリンから見た不思議おもしろ音楽事情 気分はカプリッチョ』 不思議でおもしろいヨーロッパのクラシック音楽事情を知れば、音楽の聴き方・楽しみ方がもっとわかる！ 演奏会の正しいドレスコード、アフター・コンサートの食事問題の解決法、有名オペラ歌手の舞台衣装を買える？、クラシックに知識は必要か？、音楽批評が必要な理由、コロナ禍が音楽界に与えた影響、ポストCD時代にはなにが起こる？、ハーディングはなぜパイロットになったのか？、カラヤンやバーンスタインの知られざるエピソード、シューマンの歌曲に秘められた想い――などなど、硬軟織り交ぜた音楽にまつわるさまざまなテーマを、長年にわたってベルリンで音楽評論家・音楽ジャーナリストとして活動する著者ならではの親しみやすい文章で綴る。現地だからこそわかるベルリン・フィルの話題もたっぷり。きっと誰かに話したくなる、楽しく読めてためになる、クラシック・ファン必読の一冊！ items.body:
JJ Lin, The Killers and Lana Del Rey headline this year’s Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix, but there’s plenty more music to explore across the circuit. Taking place from 9 to 11 October at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, the race weekend also brings together Indonesian indie pop, Japanese guitar rock, British jazz and home-grown favourites.

Whether you’re after an afternoon dance session or a band to add to your daily rotation, here are eight acts worth making time for between the racing action and headline sets.

Coldiac

When: 9 October, 9.30PM to 10.15PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Indie pop, R&B and synth-pop

Indonesian trio Coldiac make an appealing case for staying out a little longer. Their music brings together pop hooks, R&B influences and synths, offering plenty for listeners who like their indie pop with a groove.

Tracks such as ‘Wreck This Journal’ and ‘TARA’ helped introduce the band, whose catalogue has since expanded to include Lemons Made Lemonade and singles ‘Eksplorasi’ and ‘Jangan Pernah Berubah’. Their 2025 EP Loving You Like This also sees them put their own spin on Indonesian classics. For newcomers, that mix of original material and reinterpretations offers several routes into their sound ahead of Friday’s set.

KIKI

When: 10 October, 6PM to 6.45PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Synth-pop, nu-disco and dreamy dance music

Bangkok trio KIKI make music for anyone who likes a little introspection with their dancing. Their sound moves between guitar pop, funk, nu-disco and electronic textures, pairing reflective songwriting with rhythms that keep things moving.

Singapore listeners may recognise them from Baybeats, while their festival appearances also include Japan’s Fuji Rock and France’s Les Escales. Get acquainted through Post Existential Crisis or Death of a Daisy & Birth of an Oyster, then check out this year’s ‘Wait a Minute’. Their Saturday evening slot makes them a tempting stop for fans looking to explore Thailand’s indie scene.

Ezra Collective

When: 10 October, 3.45PM to 4.30PM

Where: Downtown, Zone 4

For fans of: Jazz, Afrobeat, hip-hop and a proper dance session

Bring your dancing shoes for Ezra Collective. The British quintet’s music draws jazz, Afrobeat, hip-hop and soul into performances built around rhythm and collective movement. Their album Where I’m Meant To Be earned them the Mercury Prize, and they bring that expansive sound to an early Saturday set.

Dance, No One’s Watching is a particularly good introduction to their approach. Try ‘God Gave Me Feet for Dancing’ and ‘Ajala’ before heading down. Drummer Femi Koleoso has spoken about shaping the band’s music around the momentum of a dance floor, and that spirit carries into their live shows, where getting the audience involved is central to the experience. Arrive ready to move.

Pleasantry

When: 10 October, 4PM to 4.45PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Dreamy indie music and intricate guitars

Singapore indie favourites Pleasantry reward those who listen closely. The quintet’s appeal lies in the interplay: guitars winding around each other, shifting rhythmic patterns and warm melodies that give their intricate arrangements an inviting centre.

Since Synapses, they’ve remained active on the gig circuit, taking their music overseas and letting songs evolve through years of performances. Their 2025 album Slow Burn captures that patient approach, but the real draw here is catching those musical conversations onstage. Try ‘Constellation’ and ‘Quiet’ before heading down, then listen for how the individual parts come together.

Lola Amour

When: 11 October, 4.30PM to 5.15PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Funk-pop, Filipino indie and communal singalongs

You may already know ‘Raining in Manila’. Sunday is your chance to get better acquainted with Lola Amour, the Manila band behind it and fellow favourite ‘Fallen’. Their mix of pop, funk and rock makes them an accessible starting point for anyone looking to explore contemporary Filipino music.

There’s plenty of evidence that their songs come into their own with a crowd. At shows previously covered by Bandwagon, fans have sung back lyrics, joined in with ad-libs and jumped through instrumental breaks. ‘Raining in Manila’ even brought the band onstage with Chris Martin during Coldplay’s Philippine visit in 2024. Come with the chorus learnt, and leave with a few more songs to look up.

TOKiMONSTA

When: 9 October, 3.15PM to 4.15PM

Where: Barge Stage, Zone 1

For fans of: Electronic music, R&B and adventurous production

TOKiMONSTA gives Zone 1 ticketholders a reason to arrive early on Friday. The GRAMMY-nominated producer’s catalogue stretches from Midnight Menu to Eternal Reverie, bringing electronic experimentation into conversation with R&B and a wide range of collaborators, including Anderson .Paak, Yuna and ZHU.

For a taste of that range, start with Eternal Reverie. Its tracks move through disco-pop, soul and quieter instrumental passages, with ‘Lucky U’ and ‘On Sum’ offering two very different entry points. That breadth makes her an intriguing pick for listeners who enjoy following a producer across genres.

Polkadot Stingray

When: 11 October, 6.45PM to 7.30PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Japanese rock and nimble guitar work

If guitar bands are your priority, put Polkadot Stingray on your list. Led by vocalist and guitarist Shizuku, the Japanese quartet have built their identity around tightly arranged rock songs, sharp guitar work and an assertive stage presence.

‘Telecaster Stripe’ and ‘Electric Public’ are useful starting points before their Sunday appearance. Shizuku also takes a central role in the band’s songwriting, design and video production, giving listeners a whole visual world to explore alongside the music. At the circuit, though, the draw is straightforward: a chance to hear those intricate arrangements delivered live.

Momocurly

When: 9 October, 5.45PM to 6.30PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: City pop, jazz and atmospheric indie

For a discovery that might take you somewhere unexpected, try Momocurly. The Tokyo-based French-Japanese duo bring together city pop, jazz, indie pop and ambient sounds, drawing on both Tokyo’s underground music scene and French influences.

They also handle the entire recording process themselves, from writing and performing to mixing and mastering. Their music’s combination of grooves and spacious textures makes this a promising pick for listeners who enjoy the softer, dreamier corners of pop. Catch them on Friday evening and give yourself 45 minutes to settle into their world.

Tickets can be purchased through the official Singapore Grand Prix website. Check that your ticket covers the day and access zone of your chosen performances. Plan accordingly and consult the official entertainment schedule before heading down.

items._cn_summary: RootsWorld Radio第028期节目单并非乐评或专辑介绍，而是一份广播节目曲目列表。内容涉及多位艺人，包括Ursula Rucker与PRISM Quartet合作的Generate Music专辑（融合诗歌与萨克斯四重奏）、Symbio、Spectrum Quartett等当代音乐组合，以及Chief Commander Ebenezer Obey的非洲流行乐、Esther Phillips的福音灵魂乐、希腊裔艺人Grecia Alban、莫桑比克Timbila Ta Venancio的拇指琴传统音乐等多种风格。节目呈现了跨地域的音乐取样，但缺乏对任何作品的具体评述与艺术分析，信息量不足以构成完整乐评。整体偏向世界音乐与多元文化采样，但缺乏深度评论支撑。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: Tiny Sun由三位音乐人合作完成，专辑收录18首小品，总时长仅34分钟，以原声吉他、尤克里里、滑棒吉他与键盘为主，风格偏向Americana民谣。Martina Sorbara的高亮清澈人声是核心，歌词聚焦失落、爱情消逝与对世界无常的顺从。曲目受多位民谣与乡村艺人影响，如Michelle Shocked、Cowboy Parton等；部分曲目加入管风琴与弦乐，呈现电影配乐般的怀旧感。专辑创作历经多年异地合作完成，成员各自有成熟的音乐事业，包括电视剧配乐、roots乐队Dragonette及Dragonette等。三首单曲被重点推介：矿工布鲁斯风格的《Kerosene Madrigal》、灵魂乡村风格的《Imagined Love》、以及短小精悍的终曲《A Grand Expanse》。整体氛围轻柔内敛，偏向传统民谣表达方式，缺乏实验性与声音设计层面的突破。
